title: What HTML does
architecture_title: The web platform and the role of HTML
dek: Give the browser a document it can understand.
lesson:
A browser needs more than words and coordinates. It needs to know which words are a heading, which image needs an alternative, and which control submits a form. HTML supplies that structure. CSS controls presentation. JavaScript can change the document and respond to events.

Those responsibilities overlap in useful ways. A details element can open without your JavaScript. A required input can stop an ordinary form submission. You still need a server to decide whether a submitted value is acceptable. Native browser behavior gives you a starting point, not an application backend.

## Start with the content
Write the document before adding layout. In the example, the heading names a small lending library and the paragraph explains its purpose. The link already works with a keyboard and has a destination. If the stylesheet fails, the information remains available.

Your job is to describe what the page contains. Pick the element whose meaning fits the content, then style it. A very large paragraph does not become a heading because it looks like one.
code:
Neighbourhood Library

Borrow books and find a quiet place to read.

Browse the catalogue
explanation: The main element identifies the page's dominant content. The h1 names it. The anchor is a real hyperlink because it has an href. These choices remain useful without a framework, a stylesheet or a pointer device.
mistake: Using a clickable div for navigation adds work. It needs keyboard behavior, focus handling and semantics that a hyperlink already supplies.
question: Which part of this example belongs to HTML, and which change would require CSS: renaming the heading, changing its colour, or changing the link destination?
answer: The heading text and href are document content, so both are HTML changes. Colour is a presentation decision for CSS. JavaScript is unnecessary for any of these edits.
objectives: Distinguish structure from presentation
Choose a hyperlink for navigation

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: the language and its scope

title: Reading a Living Standard
architecture_title: HTML's history, evolution and Living Standard
dek: Look up a rule without treating every browser as identical.
lesson:
The HTML Living Standard changes over time. A reference to HTML5 often describes the modern language informally; it does not identify a frozen collection of features you can assume every browser supports.

The Standard contains authoring requirements, browser processing rules, explanations and indexes. The index is useful for finding a feature. Its summaries are not substitutes for the feature's actual definition. Read the definition when nesting, defaults or exceptions affect your example.

## Separate three questions
Ask whether the markup conforms, whether your target browsers implement the behavior, and whether your use is accessible and appropriate. These questions need different evidence. A new element can be in the Standard while implementation remains uneven. An old presentational element can still render while being nonconforming for authors.

The example uses a normal document declaration. There is no version number to update when you use a newer conforming feature. Record the relevant source and review date in your project notes instead. Compatibility data is a dated aid, not a promise about a visitor's installed software.
code: Library notes
explanation: The doctype is the short HTML doctype. It does not opt into a named annual release. The language, encoding and title solve separate document concerns.
mistake: Using successful rendering as the only test of conformance. Browsers deliberately recover from many authoring errors.
question: An obsolete element displays in your browser. Is that enough evidence to recommend it in new markup?
answer: No. Rendering support can exist for old content. Check the authoring requirements and use a conforming replacement that preserves the intended meaning. Then check the replacement in the browsers you support.
objectives: Distinguish authoring rules from implementation support
Find a definition beyond the index

title: From source to page
architecture_title: How browsers interpret web documents
dek: The text file and the browser document are related, but different.
lesson:
The server sends bytes with a media type. For a text/html response, the browser decodes those bytes and runs the HTML parser. Parsing creates nodes in a document tree. Styles and layout then determine how that tree is presented.

Scripts can change the tree after parsing. Developer Tools usually shows the current tree, not a faithful printout of the file you saved. View Source and the Elements panel answer different questions.

## Follow one change
Our example gives a paragraph an id. A script can find the element and change its text. The original response still contains the old wording. A test that inspects the current DOM should expect the changed wording after that script has run.

The browser may also add implied elements and repair certain malformed structures during parsing. Do not take the repaired tree as permission to keep broken source. Find the authoring error, correct the source, and test again. Keep network failures separate from parsing failures: a valid document can still refer to an unavailable resource.
code: Opening hours are being checked.
explanation: The script runs after the paragraph has been parsed because it appears after that paragraph. textContent sets text, so the replacement string is not parsed as markup.
mistake: Assuming a selector can find a later element before the parser has created it. Script placement and loading behavior affect timing.
question: What will View Source show after the paragraph changes, and what will the current DOM show?
answer: View Source shows the response containing the original sentence. The current DOM contains the updated text node. A later reload can produce the same change again because the script runs again.
objectives: Describe the path from bytes to nodes
Distinguish response source from the live DOM

title: Elements, tags and attributes
architecture_title: Elements, tags, attributes and content
dek: Name the parts before debugging the page.
lesson:
An element is part of the document. Tags are syntax used to write many elements in HTML source. Most ordinary elements have a start tag, contents and an end tag. Some, such as img and input, are void elements and do not have end tags.

An attribute adds information to an element's start tag. In our link, href gives the destination and class provides a token for styling or scripting. Neither attribute changes the element into another kind of element.

## Read the whole element
The link's accessible wording comes from its text in this simple case. A class such as button does not supply button semantics. If the control navigates, keep the anchor. If it performs an action in the current interface, consider a button.

Text between tags becomes text nodes. A comment is a different node and is not displayed as normal page content. Comments are still delivered to the browser. Never store passwords, private tokens or confidential project notes in them.
code: Browse available books
explanation: The start tag carries two attributes. The end tag closes the anchor. Whitespace around the words can affect text nodes, but it does not create another element.
mistake: Calling every piece of angle-bracket syntax an element. In particular, the doctype is a declaration, and an end tag is syntax rather than a second element.
question: Identify the element name, attribute names, attribute values and link text in the example.
answer: The element name is a. The attributes are class and href, with values catalogue-link and catalogue.html. The words Browse available books are the link text. The comment is separate from the anchor.
objectives: Identify tags, attributes and contents
Keep confidential information out of source

title: Think in trees
architecture_title: The DOM tree and document structure
dek: Parent and child relationships explain many markup rules.
lesson:
The DOM is a tree of nodes. The document has an element child, html, which normally contains head and body. An element can contain text and other elements where its content model allows them.

Parent, child, sibling and descendant describe relationships, not screen positions. Two boxes that sit side by side can have very different places in the tree. A heading belongs to an article because of the document structure, not because it happens to appear above it visually.

## Inspect one branch
Here the article is a child of main. The heading and paragraph are siblings. The em element is a child of the paragraph and a descendant of the article. A selector or a DOM method operates on these relationships.

Keep the tree understandable before styling. Deep wrappers can be appropriate, but each extra layer should have a reason. Do not use the visual layout as evidence that nesting is valid: a browser can display invalidly nested source after repairing it.
code:
A shelf for local writers

Bring a book by an independent author.
explanation: The emphasis belongs inside the sentence. Moving em around the whole article would change both the semantics and the validity question; phrasing elements cannot simply wrap arbitrary document sections.
mistake: Assuming that any element may contain any other element as long as the end tags match.
question: Is em a direct child of article? Are h1 and p siblings?
answer: em is not a direct child of article; p is its parent. h1 and p share article as a parent, so they are siblings. Both are descendants of main.
objectives: Describe parent, sibling and descendant relationships
Separate visual arrangement from document structure

title: Make your first document
architecture_title: Setting up a development environment and creating a first page
dek: Use a text editor, a browser and a small feedback loop.
lesson:
Create a folder with index.html. Save it as UTF-8, then open it in a browser. A local file is enough for the first static document. Later, use a local HTTP server for examples that depend on fetch, modules, origin behavior or server responses.

Use an editor that lets you see the actual file contents. A rich-text document renamed with an html extension is not an HTML source file. Confirm that your operating system has not quietly saved index.html.txt.

## Check what you changed
Edit one heading, save, reload, and find the changed text. Open Developer Tools and inspect the heading. Change the document title and look at the browser tab. These separate checks establish where your output appears.

Run a conformance checker early. Fix errors in the smallest document before adding layout. Keep a copy you can return to, preferably in version control. Browser extensions can alter pages, so use a clean profile when investigating behavior you cannot explain.
code:
A good place to start reading

Visit the library on Saturday.
explanation: The viewport declaration supports a page sized for a device's viewport. It is not a responsive layout by itself. The page still needs CSS if its later layout should adapt to available space.
mistake: Editing a different copy of the file from the one open in the browser. Check the address and the saved path before debugging the markup.
question: Change the tab title without changing the visible heading. Which element should you edit?
answer: Edit title inside head. The visible heading is h1 inside body. They may use different wording because one labels the document in browser UI while the other introduces the page content.
objectives: Create a complete UTF-8 HTML document
Verify changes in the browser and a checker

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: a quick introduction

title: The document shell
architecture_title: HTML document anatomy and the doctype
dek: Give each document a predictable beginning.
lesson:
A complete HTML page normally declares the doctype, document language, encoding, title and body content. This small shell is worth understanding even if your framework generates it.

The doctype helps select standards-mode processing. It is not an instruction to fetch a document type definition. The html element is the document element. head holds document metadata; body holds the document's content.

## Avoid copying a shell blindly
Set lang to the language actually used by the page. Keep the character encoding declaration early in the document; the Standard requires a meta encoding declaration to be entirely within the first 1024 bytes when that mechanism is used. A server can also communicate encoding through its response headers.

Do not duplicate head or body to combine two pages. Combine their appropriate content into a single document, resolving conflicting metadata. A stylesheet, script or template system does not excuse an invalid outer structure.
code:
Opening hours

Tuesday to Saturday, 10:00 to 17:00.
explanation: The title identifies this page and its site. The heading can stay shorter. Neither substitutes for the other.
mistake: Putting a second doctype and a second body inside an existing body when pasting a complete example.
question: You receive two complete HTML files and want a single page. Should you paste the second html element inside the first body?
answer: No. Keep one document shell. Move the second page's relevant body content into the first body, choose the required metadata, then check heading structure, duplicate ids and links.
objectives: Explain the job of the doctype
Combine content without duplicating document structure

title: html, head and body
architecture_title: The html, head and body elements
dek: Keep metadata and page content in their intended places.
lesson:
head is not a hidden drawer for arbitrary markup. Its content model is metadata content, with additional rules for elements such as title and base. Put a visible navigation bar in body, even if it appears at the top of the screen.

body is the main container for the document's page content. The name header refers to introductory content in body; it is not a replacement for head. A page can have a document head and several meaningful headers in its content.

## Set the page language
The lang attribute on html establishes the language for descendants that do not override it. Mark a phrase in another language on an appropriate containing element. Do not use a country code when you mean a language code. A region subtag can qualify a language where it helps, but it is optional when a general language tag is enough.

Optional-tag rules can allow some tags to be omitted in carefully defined situations. Explicit html, head and body tags are a useful convention for teaching and maintenance. Understand that this is a convention, not a claim that omission is always invalid.
code:
Neighbourhood Library

Become a member
explanation: The header contains site introduction inside body. head contains metadata that describes the document.
mistake: Using head where header was intended, or assuming that body must begin immediately with a heading and cannot contain a site header.
question: Where should a site logo link go: head, header in body, or title?
answer: Put the visible logo link in body, often inside a header. title contains text for the document title, not a visible linked logo. head is for metadata.
objectives: Place metadata and visible content correctly
Set an appropriate document language

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: the document element

title: Text, encoding and escaping
architecture_title: Character encoding, Unicode and character references
dek: Make the bytes and the intended characters agree.
lesson:
UTF-8 represents characters as bytes. Your editor's save encoding and the document's declared encoding must agree. A declaration cannot repair bytes that were saved incorrectly.

Use literal readable text for ordinary characters when your workflow supports UTF-8. Character references are useful when source syntax would otherwise be ambiguous. Write < to show a less-than sign in text, and use & where an ampersand needs escaping. Escape the quote character that delimits an attribute value when it appears inside that value.

## Preserve meaning when showing code
The example displays the text <button> without creating a button. The parser consumes the character references and creates text characters. This is different from inserting untrusted strings through innerHTML, which invokes markup parsing.

A non-breaking space changes line-breaking behavior. Do not scatter it through text to imitate layout. CSS is the right place for gaps between interface elements. When you copy source between tools, check for accidental invisible characters and preserve meaningful language characters.
code:
Write <button> for an action.

Research & reading

A quoted greeting
explanation: The code element supplies semantics for a code fragment; escaping stops the fragment from being parsed as an actual element. Both decisions matter.
mistake: Escaping the same text twice. &lt; displays the reference spelling < rather than the intended less-than sign.
question:
How would you show the literal source text

Hello

inside a code element?
answer: Use <p>Hello</p> in the HTML source. The browser displays the tag spelling as text. Keep the code element so that the kind of text is still identified.
objectives: Keep saved encoding and declared encoding consistent
Escape markup when displaying source

title: Nesting and void elements
architecture_title: Nesting, void elements and optional tags
dek: Well-formed-looking tags are only the beginning.
lesson:
Close nested elements in the reverse order you opened them. That keeps the source understandable, but correct nesting also depends on each element's content model. A paragraph cannot contain arbitrary flow content such as a div.

Void elements have no contents in HTML syntax. Examples include img, br, meta, link and input. Do not write an img end tag. A trailing slash on a void element is unnecessary in HTML and does not give it XML semantics.

## Choose explicit source while learning
Some end tags can be omitted under specific conditions. Closing them explicitly is often easier to review. Other end tags, such as an anchor's end tag, are not optional in the same way.

Do not use a slash on a non-void element as if it closed the element in text/html. A script element still requires an end tag. If parsing produces an unexpected tree, inspect the source around the earliest error rather than adding more closing tags at the bottom.
code:
Bring a current membership card.

Ask at the desk if you need a replacement.
explanation: The strong element closes before its paragraph. The img stands on its own as a void element. Its width and height describe the intended intrinsic dimensions or aspect-ratio basis for layout, not a guarantee that CSS cannot resize it.
mistake: Writing <div /> in an HTML document and expecting later content to be outside the div.
question:
Why is

Notice

not a sound way to put a notice box inside a paragraph?
answer: A div is not permitted paragraph content. The HTML parser can close the paragraph before it processes the div, producing a tree unlike the source suggests. Use a containing div or section with a paragraph inside it instead.
objectives: Recognize void elements
Check content rules as well as matching tags

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: elements and tag omission

title: Attributes and their values
architecture_title: Attributes, quoting, whitespace and comments
dek: Presence, an empty string and the word false are different things.
lesson:
Quote attribute values consistently. HTML allows unquoted values only when they satisfy its restrictions; quoting is easier to maintain when a value later gains a space or punctuation.

Boolean attributes represent their state by presence or absence. disabled="false" still supplies disabled. To leave a control enabled, omit the attribute. An enumerated attribute uses defined keywords and can have missing-value and invalid-value defaults. Do not apply boolean rules to an attribute merely because its value looks like true or false.

## Learn the value type
hidden, contenteditable and autocomplete do not all share the same value rules. Read the definition for the attribute and its particular element or state. Values such as ids, token lists, URLs and numbers each have their own syntax.

In HTML documents, attribute names on HTML elements are treated in an ASCII case-insensitive way during parsing. Lowercase names are a readable convention. Attribute values are not universally case-insensitive: an id and a URL path can be case-sensitive.
code:
<label for="member-email">Email</label>
<input id="member-email" name="email" type="email" required>
<button type="submit" disabled>Join the waiting list</button>
explanation: required and disabled are boolean attributes. The id and for values establish a label relationship. The type keyword selects an input state, whose rules affect validation and interface behavior.
mistake: Inventing a generic rule that every attribute can be turned off with the string false.
question: You find <button disabled="false">Save</button>. How do you make it enabled in the initial HTML?
answer: Remove disabled. The string false does not turn off a boolean attribute. If a script changes the state later, assign false to the element's disabled property or remove the attribute.
objectives: Distinguish boolean and enumerated attributes
Read attribute values according to their defined syntax

title: Content categories and models
architecture_title: Content categories and content models
dek: Use categories to understand what can go where.
lesson:
The Standard groups elements into content categories such as metadata, flow, phrasing and interactive content. Categories overlap. An element can belong to several, and membership can depend on its attributes or context.

A content model describes what an element can contain. Categories make those descriptions shorter, but they do not remove additional restrictions. A button can contain phrasing content while still prohibiting interactive descendants and descendants with tabindex.

## Transparent does not mean unrestricted
An anchor has a transparent content model in relevant contexts. Its contents must fit the surrounding context, with the anchor's own restrictions still applying. Wrapping an entire card in a link does not permit putting another link or a button inside that link.

The reference includes the captured category summaries and their exceptions. Treat these as routes to the definitions, especially for media, form-related elements and transparent models. The category table contains more rows than the commonly taught core category names because it also includes form-related groupings.
code:
The Atlas of Small Places

A walking guide to overlooked streets.
explanation: The navigation link and the action button are separate. Neither interactive control is nested inside the other. The article can still be styled as one visual card.
mistake: Wrapping a card containing buttons in one outer anchor and assuming transparent content permits every descendant.
question: Why is a button inside an anchor a problem even if both controls can be clicked with a mouse?
answer: The anchor's content restrictions disallow interactive descendants, including a button. The structure also leaves competing interactions in one region. Use separate controls with clear destinations or actions.
objectives: Use overlapping content categories
Apply extra restrictions on transparent and interactive content

title: Conformance and useful errors
architecture_title: HTML syntax, conformance and common errors
dek: Make the checker part of the feedback loop.
lesson:
A conformance checker can identify invalid nesting, missing required attributes and many syntax errors. It cannot decide whether your alternative text is useful, whether your page is easy to navigate, or whether a server validates a submission securely.

Check the complete document as well as small examples. The containing form, table or head can change what is permitted. Fix the earliest relevant error first because a parser recovery can cause several later messages.

## Classify what failed
A missing end tag, an unknown attribute and a broken resource URL are different problems. Some failures are conformance errors; some are network failures; some are mistakes in the intended behavior. Choose a check that can observe the failure you care about.

Keep intentionally invalid teaching examples separate from valid fixtures and record the expected error. A checker pass means the checked document passed that checker version and configuration. It is not a general quality certificate. If a new standardized feature triggers a message, compare the current definition with the checker's supported version before changing correct markup blindly.
code:
<form action="/membership" method="post">
  <label for="full-name">Full name</label>
  <input id="full-name" name="fullName" autocomplete="name" required>
  <button type="submit">Apply for membership</button>
</form>
explanation: A conformance check can inspect the label relationship and syntax. You still need to test actual submission handling and whether the requested name field is appropriate to the service.
mistake: Treating a clean checker output as proof that a page meets WCAG or has no security risks.
question: A document validates, but its submit button sends data to the wrong endpoint. Is the checker broken?
answer: No. A syntactically valid action URL can be the wrong application destination. Test the request and server behavior in addition to conformance. Each check needs a defined responsibility.
objectives: Use checker output without overclaiming
Separate syntax, network and behavior failures

title: Headings and paragraphs
architecture_title: Headings, paragraphs, thematic breaks and heading-level features
dek: Make the page structure readable without its styling.
lesson:
A heading names the content that follows it. Use h1 through h6 to express the hierarchy you intend. For the ordinary pages in this book, one page-level h1 and properly nested subsection headings are a practical convention.

Choose heading levels for structure, not font size. CSS can make an h2 smaller or larger without changing its meaning. A section element does not automatically reset a conventional heading hierarchy to a new h1 in the way many old tutorials suggested.

## Separate paragraphs from line breaks
Use p for paragraphs. br is a line break within content where the break itself belongs, such as an address or a poem. Empty paragraphs and repeated br elements are not layout tools. hr represents a thematic break, not merely a horizontal line to decorate a page.

The Living Standard also includes headingoffset and headingreset. These require independent compatibility and accessibility review; they are not a reason to discard a clear conventional hierarchy. This edition records them in the reference and uses ordinary heading levels in its running examples.
code:
Membership

Membership is open to local residents.

What to bring

Bring an address document and a form of identification.
explanation: The h2 introduces a subsection of membership. It does not depend on the browser calculating an implicit outline from section nesting.
mistake: Picking h4 because its default size matches a design. That makes document structure depend on a browser stylesheet.
question: A designer wants the main heading to look small. Should you change h1 to h5?
answer: Keep the heading level that matches the document structure and change its presentation with CSS. A visual size preference does not change where the heading belongs in the hierarchy.
objectives: Create a conventional heading hierarchy
Use paragraphs, line breaks and thematic breaks for their meanings

title: Inline meaning
architecture_title: Inline semantics, emphasis and quotations
dek: Pick emphasis because of the sentence, not the browser font.
lesson:
em marks stress emphasis. strong marks importance, seriousness or urgency. Their default italic and bold styles are not their definitions. A book title can use cite; a short quotation can use q. Use a blockquote for a quoted section rather than a short inline quotation.

small suits side comments such as a copyright or a qualification. mark can identify text relevant to the reader's current context, such as a search match. span supplies a generic phrasing container when no more specific semantic element fits.

## Do not turn typography into semantics
The b and i elements also have defined uses beyond their default appearance. b can draw attention without conveying extra importance; i can mark text in an alternate voice or mood. u is for an explicitly rendered non-textual annotation, not a generic request to underline.

Quote and cite carefully. A cite attribute can record a source URL, but browsers do not normally expose it as a useful visible citation. Provide an ordinary visible source link when readers need to follow it. cite represents a work's title rather than a person's name.
code:
Return the key before closing time.

You may borrow two reference books.

Our reading group chose Things Fall Apart.
explanation: The importance of returning the key differs from the stress on two. The novel's title names a work; it does not claim emphasis in the sentence.
mistake: Using strong around every visually bold fragment, including purely decorative interface text.
question: Which element fits a short phrase that must carry stress in the sentence, and which fits an urgent warning?
answer: Use em for stress emphasis and strong for an urgent or important warning. If the requirement is only a typeface change, use CSS on an appropriate existing element or a neutral span.
objectives: Distinguish stress, importance and presentation
Represent titles and quotations deliberately

title: Code and technical text
architecture_title: Code, technical text and machine-readable values
dek: Preserve the source when readers need to copy it.
lesson:
code identifies computer code. pre preserves the significance of whitespace in preformatted text. Combine them when indentation and line breaks matter. Escape markup characters before placing HTML source inside either element.

kbd marks user input, samp marks sample output, and var marks a variable. These meanings are useful even when a stylesheet makes them look similar. A filename or a command does not need a decorative badge to be understandable.

## Give examples enough context
State the file, command environment or containing element that an example needs. Readers should know whether they can paste a block into a document or need to supply surrounding code. A fragment that works in body may be invalid in head.

Avoid screenshots as the only version of code. Text can be copied, searched and read by assistive technology. If a code block scrolls horizontally, make the scroll container keyboard reachable and label it. Keep the example short enough to explain; put a longer working file in the downloads.
code:
Press Ctrl + S to save.

<h1>Library catalogue</h1>

The server returned 201 Created.
explanation: The example shows HTML source as text. kbd identifies input rather than output. The status string is a sample response, not proof that this page made a request.
mistake: Pasting raw <h1> markup into code and expecting it to stay visible as source.
question: Why do you still need escaping inside pre and code?
answer: Neither element turns off ordinary HTML parsing of their contents. Escape the angle brackets so the parser creates text instead of an h1 element. pre changes whitespace handling, not the basic parsing rule.
objectives: Distinguish code, input and output
Display copyable escaped source

title: Links that go somewhere
architecture_title: Links, hyperlinks, fragments and navigation
dek: Let the destination explain the control.
lesson:
An a element with href creates a hyperlink. Give it wording that makes sense in context and a destination that does what the wording promises. A file path, a fragment and an absolute URL resolve differently.

A fragment such as #fees points to an element with a matching id in the same document. Relative URLs resolve against the document's base URL. A base element can change that resolution across the page, which makes it easy to introduce surprising navigation bugs.

## Navigation is different from an action
Use a hyperlink to go to a resource. Use a button to submit a form or perform an interface action. href="#" is not a neutral placeholder for a JavaScript button; it still has navigation behavior.

Opening a new browsing context changes the user's experience. Avoid doing it automatically without a reason. If you use target="_blank", describe the behavior where it helps and understand opener relationships. Modern anchor behavior provides implicit noopener for this target, but explicitly writing rel="noopener" can document the intention. Do not imply that this solves every trust or privacy concern.
code:
Browse the catalogue

Read the membership fees

Membership fees

Ask the desk about the current membership options.
explanation: The first URL is a sibling document. The second is a fragment in this document. The target id must be unique in the element's tree.
mistake: Using link text such as click here repeatedly when a destination-specific phrase would be clearer.
question: Would you use an anchor or a button to open the next page of the catalogue? What about removing a book from a local reading list?
answer: Use an anchor for another catalogue page. Use a button for the removal action. If the action changes server data, also design and test its request, permissions and error handling; the element choice alone does not implement those controls.
objectives: Choose links for navigation
Resolve document and fragment URLs correctly

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: the a element

title: Lists with a reason
architecture_title: Ordered, unordered and description lists
dek: Order and relationships determine the markup.
lesson:
Use ul for a group whose order is not significant, and ol when sequence or rank is part of the meaning. Each item is an li. A navigation menu is often a list of links, but not every group of adjacent items needs list markup.

A description list uses dl, dt and dd for name-value groups. A group can have multiple terms or multiple descriptions. It is not limited to dictionary definitions and does not require a table-like visual layout.

## Keep nested lists inside an item
A sublist belongs inside the li it expands. A list placed beside an li is not that item's nested list. Markup should explain the relationship before CSS adds indentation.

For ordered lists, start and reversed can change the numbering behavior, and an li value can set an item's ordinal value in an ol. These are useful when the displayed order has meaning. Avoid using list markers as a substitute for actual text if readers need the text outside that presentation.
code:
1. Choose a book.
  2. Check the lending period.
    • Reference books have separate rules.
  3. Take the book to the desk.
explanation: The unordered sublist qualifies the second step. It remains inside that step's li, so the tree preserves the relationship.
mistake: Putting the nested ul directly under the outer ol between two li elements.
question: Which structure fits opening hours grouped by day names: an ordered list of steps or a description list?
answer: A description list is a reasonable choice for day names and their hours because the groups describe name-value relationships. A table may be better when readers need to compare a regular grid of days and multiple time ranges. An ordered list would imply a meaningful sequence of steps.
objectives: Distinguish ordered, unordered and description lists
Nest a list under the item it expands

title: Figures and captions
architecture_title: Figures, captions and self-contained content
dek: Keep self-contained material with its explanation.
lesson:
A figure holds self-contained content that the surrounding prose can refer to as a unit. It can contain a diagram, photograph, code listing or another suitable item. figcaption supplies its caption as the first or last child when present.

Not every image needs a figure. An icon in a button is part of that control. A photograph beside a paragraph may or may not be self-contained. Decide from the content relationship, not a desire for a styled border.

## A caption and alternative text do different work
A caption explains the figure in the document. Alternative text supplies a replacement for an image according to its purpose and context. Repeating a long caption word for word as alt can add noise without helping. An image with information absent from the caption still needs that information represented appropriately.

A complex chart usually needs more than a short alt string. Provide the important conclusion and a detailed text or data alternative that readers can reach. Do not claim an image is accessible solely because alt is present.
explanation: The alternative conveys the directions shown by the image. The caption identifies the figure's subject in the document. A real floor plan would need its own reviewed alternative based on its actual contents.
mistake: Generating alternative text from a filename without inspecting the image or its purpose.
question: A chart caption says Monthly loans. Does repeating Monthly loans in alt communicate the chart's trend?
answer: No. It only repeats the subject. Describe the meaningful information, and provide an accessible data table or fuller explanation when the chart needs one. The appropriate wording depends on the actual data and the reason the chart appears.
objectives: Choose a figure for self-contained content
Separate a caption from an image alternative

title: Dates, values and edits
architecture_title: Dates, times, abbreviations and document edits
dek: Give machines a useful value without spoiling the sentence.
lesson:
time can pair readable date or time text with a machine-readable datetime value. Use a value that matches the defined syntax and the kind of temporal information you actually know. Do not add a timezone or a time of day just to make a date look more precise.

data associates its contents with a machine-readable value. It is useful for a product identifier or another mapping that a script or processor uses. It does not create a general validation rule for that value.

## Record edits when the change matters
ins and del mark additions and deletions. Their datetime and cite attributes can record when and why a change happened, subject to their defined rules. Provide visible context when readers need it; an attribute alone is not a usable change log.

s has a different meaning from del: it marks content that is no longer accurate or relevant, without necessarily marking a document edit. An old price can be struck through while the current price remains plainly stated. Choose the meaning before choosing the decoration.
code:
Next meeting: 7 November 2026.

Book code: Local history collection.

The desk opens at 09:00 10:00.
explanation: The date supplies only a date. The collection has an explicit identifier. The changed opening time is visible in the sentence, rather than hidden in metadata.
mistake: Writing an informal date such as 7/11/26 in datetime and assuming every parser will interpret it the same way.
question: You know an event date but not its time. Should you write a midnight UTC timestamp?
answer: No. Use a valid date value such as 2026-11-07. A fabricated time or timezone adds information you do not have and can mislead downstream software.
objectives: Use machine-readable dates without invented precision
Distinguish document edits from obsolete wording

title: Language and direction
architecture_title: International text, bidirectional text and language semantics
dek: Language, writing direction and pronunciation are separate concerns.
lesson:
Set the primary language on html, then mark language changes where they occur. A valid language tag helps software choose pronunciation, spelling and other language-sensitive behavior. It does not translate the words or determine their writing direction.

Use dir for directionality. Values such as rtl and ltr express known directions; auto lets the user agent determine direction from the content under the defined rules. For user-provided names or messages of unknown direction, isolation can stop adjacent punctuation and text from being rearranged unexpectedly.

## Work with unfamiliar text
bdi isolates a run of text from the surrounding bidirectional context. bdo overrides direction and is a more specialized tool, not the normal choice for ordinary right-to-left text. Avoid inserting directional control characters casually when markup expresses the relationship more clearly.

Ruby annotations use ruby with rt and, where appropriate, rp fallback punctuation. They have language-specific uses and should be reviewed by someone who understands the writing system. Test the actual languages your product supports, including long words, mixed scripts and names that do not fit a Western given-name/surname assumption.
code:
Readers say Ẹ káàbọ̀ at the entrance.

Reserved for مريم: shelf 4.
explanation: The first span identifies Yoruba text. The bdi isolates the Arabic name from the English sentence and its punctuation. Language metadata does not replace a correct translation or a test with the intended text. The Arabic name uses numeric character references to keep the printed source unambiguous; the browser still renders the name as Arabic text.
mistake: Using CSS direction as the only representation of document language, or assuming every non-Latin script is right-to-left.
question: A visitor submits a name whose writing direction you do not know. What is a reasonable HTML wrapper inside an English sentence?
answer: Use bdi, commonly with dir="auto", around the name. Keep the surrounding sentence language separate. Insert the untrusted name as text, not as untrusted HTML.
objectives: Mark language changes
Isolate mixed-direction text

sources.title: HTML Living Standard: language and direction

title: Containers and grouping
architecture_title: Generic containers and grouping elements
dek: Use a generic container when the content has no more specific grouping meaning.
lesson:
div is a generic flow container. span is its phrasing-level counterpart. Both are useful. The problem is replacing meaningful elements with them automatically, or adding layers with no clear purpose.

A wrapper for a layout grid may be a div. An independent article can be article. A quoted passage belongs in blockquote. Keep these choices distinct from class names such as card, row and panel, which describe your implementation rather than defining HTML semantics.

## Group for a stated reason
Start with the text and controls, then add a wrapper only when layout, scripting or a content relationship needs one. A single element can carry several class tokens. You do not need a separate div for every CSS property.

Do not add a role to every generic container. Many wrappers should remain semantically neutral. Adding unnecessary landmarks or groups can make an interface harder to navigate with assistive technology. When you do add an explicit accessible group, give it an appropriate purpose and name and test that relationship.
code:
Visit the library

Ask at reception for directions.

Call the desk

Call our example number
explanation: The outer div is a layout wrapper. The named sections carry the content organization. The telephone number is fictional and must be replaced before publishing a real contact page.
mistake: Naming a div class="section" and assuming it now has section semantics.
question: A wrapper exists only to arrange two existing sections in a grid. Does it need to become a third section?
answer: No. A generic div is appropriate for the layout wrapper. Another section would imply another thematic grouping and should have a content reason.
objectives: Use generic wrappers deliberately
Avoid adding semantics without a content reason

title: Sections that have a subject
architecture_title: Semantic regions and document organization
dek: A section should explain the document, not a spacing requirement.
lesson:
section represents a thematic grouping, normally with a heading. A chapter's requirements, an article's background and a service page's eligibility rules can be sections. A border or a margin does not establish a theme.

A heading can be enough to structure a straightforward document without wrapping every subsection in section. Choose wrappers when they clarify grouping or are needed for the document's relationships. Keep the conventional heading hierarchy readable either way.

## Name important regions
A section with an accessible name can become a region landmark in relevant accessibility mappings. Name a region when users benefit from navigating to it, rather than naming every small block. aria-labelledby can reference an existing visible heading.

Source order should remain understandable when layout is removed. Moving columns with CSS does not change the DOM reading order. Review both the visible result and the underlying sequence, especially when the page has multiple related sections.
code:
Who can join

Membership options depend on the service you need.

Young readers

A guardian can help complete the application.
explanation: The section has a theme and a visible heading used as its name. The h3 is a subsection under the h2, not a visual size instruction.
mistake: Replacing every div with section as a general cleanup step.
question: A block exists solely to add a background colour around two unrelated widgets. Should it automatically be a section?
answer: No. A div may be the more accurate wrapper. Use section when the content forms a thematic grouping, usually introduced by a heading.
objectives: Identify a thematic grouping
Name useful regions without excessive landmarks

title: Articles and supporting content
architecture_title: Articles, sections, headers, footers and asides
dek: Decide what can stand on its own.
lesson:
article represents a complete or self-contained composition that could be distributed or reused independently in principle. A news story, a forum post or a self-contained review can qualify. An article can contain its own header, footer and sections.

aside holds content tangentially related to its surrounding content. The element does not mean right column. Related background could appear beneath the article on a phone and still be an aside. address provides contact information for its nearest relevant article or body ancestor; it is not a generic postal-address styling element.

## Reuse header and footer carefully
header is introductory or navigational material for its relevant context. footer can contain authorship, related links or other footer information. A footer does not need to sit at the bottom of a viewport.

Keep a page's repeated site header separate from an article's own introduction. If you include dates, author details or related reading, make their relationship clear from the surrounding structure and text. Do not select article merely because a card has a title; ask whether the content is a composition in its own right.
code:
A reading room after school

Library programme notes

The room is available for supervised study.

Contact the library desk for current sessions.
explanation: The article includes its own introduction and footer. Their meaning belongs to this composition; a page may also have a separate site-wide header and footer.
mistake: Using aside because a design puts something on the right, even when it contains essential main content.
question: Is the only set of instructions for submitting an application appropriate in an aside?
answer: Usually not. Those instructions are part of the main task, not tangential content. Put essential instructions with the form or the relevant main section.
objectives: Distinguish standalone and tangential content
Use contextual headers and footers

title: Navigation and main content
architecture_title: Navigation, landmarks and main content
dek: Give recurring page regions clear jobs.
lesson:
main represents the dominant content of the document body. A normal visible page should not expose several competing main regions. Repeated site navigation and the general site footer ordinarily sit outside main.

nav identifies a major navigation section. Use it for the principal site menu or a substantial table of contents, not every isolated link. If several navigation regions need distinguishing, give them concise names such as Primary and On this page.

## Make repeated content easy to pass
A skip link near the beginning can take keyboard users to main content. Its target needs a unique id and should be tested in the browsers you support. Keep the link visible on focus rather than hiding it permanently.

The search element groups controls or content used for searching or filtering. It does not implement a search service by itself. A form inside it can submit a query to a real endpoint. Keep the form's label and response behavior usable without relying on a decorative magnifying-glass icon.
code:
Skip to main content
Home Catalogue

Library services

Choose a service from the catalogue.
explanation: The skip destination is programmatically focusable without adding it to ordinary sequential keyboard navigation. Test actual focus and scrolling rather than assuming the fragment provides the full intended experience everywhere.
mistake: Giving several visible main elements different class names and treating them as layout columns.
question: How would you distinguish a site menu from a chapter table of contents for landmark navigation?
answer: Use separate nav regions and name them, for example Primary and On this page. Keep names concise and avoid repeating the word navigation when the role already communicates it.
objectives: Create a clear main region
Distinguish navigation regions and test a skip link

title: Tables that explain the data
architecture_title: Tables, captions, headers and accessible data relationships
dek: Use a table when the relationships run in rows and columns.
lesson:
A data table relates cells along two axes. Use table, tr and the appropriate th or td cells. A caption identifies the table. thead, tbody and tfoot can group rows, but grouping alone does not create header associations for every complex layout.

For a simple table, use scope="col" on column headers and scope="row" on row headers where appropriate. More complex tables can need explicit id and headers relationships. Simplifying the data layout is often easier for readers than making a deeply spanned table navigable.

## Preserve the relationships on small screens
A wide table can live in a labelled, keyboard-reachable scrolling region. Do not replace it with a screenshot. If you change its visual layout, test that header relationships and reading order still make sense.

rowspan and colspan change the cell grid. Incorrect spans can make a table model hard to reason about even when the display appears close enough. Do not use obsolete presentational attributes to recreate an old layout system. Use CSS for table styling and keep HTML focused on the data.
code:
Lending periods
CollectionDays
General lending14
Reference desk copies0
explanation: Each value has a collection row header and a Days column header. The numbers are fictional teaching data, not actual library policy.
mistake: Using a table for an entire page layout, or using bold td cells where actual th headers are required.
question: Which two headers should describe the value 14 in this table?
answer: General lending and Days. The row header supplies the category and the column header supplies the quantity. The caption identifies the table as lending-period data.
objectives: Build a simple data table with headers
Recognize when a complex table needs stronger associations

title: Plan a small site
architecture_title: Designing complete multi-page document structures
dek: Page structure should survive the trip between documents.
lesson:
Before writing a multi-page site, list the pages and the task each page supports. Give every document a distinct title and a useful main heading. Repeated navigation should remain consistent without making every page's content identical.

Use relative links deliberately. A path from pages/contact.html to the home page differs from the same path in index.html. A root-relative path beginning with a slash can break when the site is hosted under a repository subpath on GitHub Pages.

## Work from a content map
For the library, start with Home, Catalogue, Membership and Contact. Keep policy wording in one maintained location and link to it. If pages repeat the same structure, use a build template rather than manually copying it indefinitely.

A navigation link with aria-current="page" identifies the current page. Keep that state correct on each document. Do not rely only on colour to mark it visually. Test every relative path from the built output and from the eventual deployment base path.
code: Home Catalogue Membership Contact
explanation: The current-page state belongs to the catalogue link on this page. A shared template needs page-specific information to put that state on the right link.
mistake: Assuming a site that works at localhost / will work unchanged at /repository-name/ when links begin with a slash.
question: From pages/contact.html, what relative path reaches index.html one directory above?
answer: Use ../index.html. The double-dot segment moves to the parent directory. Check the built link rather than guessing from the source template path.
objectives: Assign a purpose to each page
Test paths under a deployment subdirectory

title: Images with a purpose
architecture_title: Images, alternative text and image dimensions
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: The alternative depends on why the image is there.
lesson:
An img embeds an image. Its src identifies a resource; alt supplies a text alternative according to the image's purpose. Useful alternative text requires the actual image and its context. A filename or a generic image description is not enough evidence.

For a purely decorative image, alt="" can keep it out of the ordinary text alternative. Do not omit alt as a casual way to say decorative. A functional image in a link needs an alternative that communicates the link's purpose if no other accessible wording provides it.

## Reserve the space
Provide width and height when you know the intended image dimensions or ratio. CSS can still size the rendered image responsively. Reserving an aspect ratio helps avoid layout movement as the resource loads.

Use loading="lazy" for suitable off-screen images, not automatically for the likely largest above-the-fold image. decoding and fetchpriority are hints with defined behavior and implementation limits. Measure before claiming a performance improvement. A broken src and a valid alt are different tests: an alternative does not make a missing image resource successful.
explanation: This teaching image needs a real file with matching content and dimensions before use. The wording describes its supposed informational purpose; it is not a universal alt string to reuse for any photograph.
mistake: Writing alt="image" or alt="photo" while leaving out the information the image contributes.
question: An image repeats the adjacent text label inside the same link and adds no other information. What alt value may be appropriate?
answer: An empty alt can avoid repeating the link label, provided the visible text already supplies the required name and the image is genuinely redundant. Review the complete link and context rather than applying this to all linked images.
objectives: Choose alternatives from purpose and context
Use dimensions and loading hints deliberately

title: Responsive image choices
architecture_title: Responsive images: picture, source, srcset and sizes
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: Offer candidates without pretending the browser follows a simple width switch.
lesson:
srcset gives the browser image candidates. Width descriptors describe candidate resource widths; sizes describes the expected rendered slot width for selecting among width candidates. A misleading sizes value can cause an unnecessarily large or blurry choice.

picture is useful for art direction or format alternatives. Its source elements appear before the fallback img. The img remains required for the actual image and its alternative text. A source inside picture has rules different from a source inside audio or video.

## Match the markup to the layout
If the slot is full width on small screens and half the viewport on wider screens, describe that relationship accurately. Keep a src fallback and test actual selections in the network panel at different viewport sizes and device pixel ratios.

Do not write a fixed candidate table and promise a particular resource in every browser condition. Selection can account for implementation and device considerations. For art direction, inspect that each crop still communicates the intended content and that the single alternative text remains appropriate.

## Read the descriptors literally
A `640w` descriptor says that the candidate resource has an intrinsic width of 640 pixels. It is not a breakpoint and does not mean "use this file on a 640-pixel screen." A `2x` descriptor expresses pixel density instead. Do not mix width and density descriptors in one candidate list.

With width candidates, `sizes` describes the intended image slot, not the width of the image file. It helps resource selection; it does not set the CSS layout. Check that the layout and the declared slot agree. When testing, inspect the image's `currentSrc` as well as its rendered dimensions. A previously cached resource can affect what you observe, so one resize is not a complete loading test.
explanation: The candidates must exist and have the stated widths. sizes describes a layout assumption; change it when the actual CSS slot no longer follows that assumption.
mistake: Using width descriptors with an inaccurate sizes value, or believing srcset is a guaranteed breakpoint-to-file mapping.
question: When is picture more appropriate than simply adding more width candidates to one img?
answer: Use picture when the source itself should change, such as a different crop for a narrow layout or a supported format alternative. Use width candidates when the same image composition is available at different resource widths.
objectives: Describe candidate widths and slot size
Separate resolution switching from art direction

title: Audio, video and tracks
architecture_title: Audio, video, source, captions and tracks
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: Playable media needs controls and usable alternatives.
lesson:
audio and video embed media. Provide controls unless an appropriate alternative interface supplies the required operation. Autoplay is subject to browser policies and user choices; adding autoplay is not a guarantee that playback begins.

source provides alternate media resources with relevant type information. track supplies timed text such as captions, subtitles or descriptions using a supported format, commonly WebVTT. Captions and subtitles serve different purposes, so choose the kind accurately.

## Plan the alternative before publishing
A transcript, captions and an audio description each address different access needs. The correct combination depends on the media and the information it conveys. A decorative silent clip and an instructional interview do not have identical requirements.

Include a poster for suitable video content and choose preload with an understanding that it is a hint. Third-party players add privacy, performance and embedding-policy concerns. Test keyboard playback controls, caption selection, mobile behavior and fallback links with the actual resources. Placeholder filenames prove nothing about media decoding or caption accuracy.
code: Read the tour transcript
explanation: The track refers to a real caption file that must be written and checked against the media. The transcript link is available outside the video fallback content, so it remains visible in supporting browsers.
mistake: Treating auto-generated captions as reviewed simply because a track file loads.
question: Why put the transcript link outside the video element as well as providing fallback content?
answer: Fallback children are not a reliable always-visible location in browsers that support video. An ordinary external paragraph gives every reader a discoverable transcript link.
objectives: Provide controls and intentional loading hints
Distinguish timed text and transcript needs

title: Image maps
architecture_title: Image maps and interactive image regions
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: Coordinate-based hotspots need an equivalent way to navigate.
lesson:
An image map associates areas of an image with hyperlinks. img uses usemap to refer to a map. area supplies a shape, coordinates, destination and appropriate alternative text for each linked region.

These controls are tied to the image's coordinate system. A design that resizes or changes the image needs careful testing. For many interfaces, ordinary links beside a diagram are easier to maintain and understand.

## Explain the destinations
Give each linked area an alt that communicates its purpose. A geographic or building diagram should not require readers to identify a shape visually before they can follow a link. Provide visible text links when they make the choices clearer.

Check keyboard focus, activation and the relationship between the displayed image and the hotspot geometry. The existence of an area element does not prove that a visitor can find the right destination or that the coordinate mapping still matches a responsive design.
code: Reading room details
explanation: The usemap fragment matches the map name. The coordinates are illustrative and need to be measured against the actual 600 by 400 image.
mistake: Copying hotspot coordinates to a different image and assuming the clickable regions still match.
question: What needs to change when a replacement floor-plan image moves the reading room to another location?
answer: Review the area geometry against the new image, update coordinates and alternatives as necessary, and retest navigation. Also inspect the visible link wording and any directions that referred to the old layout.
objectives: Connect a map and its areas
Review geometry and alternatives against the actual image

title: Embedding another document
architecture_title: Iframes, embedded resources and sandboxing
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: An iframe introduces another browsing context and another trust decision.
lesson:
iframe embeds another document. Give it a useful title so readers can identify the embedded content. A title does not fix the embedded document's own accessibility problems.

sandbox restricts capabilities. The tokens you add restore particular capabilities, so start from the actual requirements and grant as little as the integration needs. Combining allow-scripts with allow-same-origin can weaken the intended isolation for same-origin content. Do not describe sandbox as a universal security wrapper.

## Consider the resource owner
Third-party embeds may load tracking, cookies, scripts and further resources. Review privacy, origin policy, referrer policy and the allow attribute's Permissions Policy integration. A provider's sample embed code is a starting point, not a completed review.

object and embed serve other embedding cases and bring their own fallback and implementation concerns. param is obsolete for authoring in the captured Standard and belongs in migration guidance. Do not add it to new object examples because an old tutorial used it.
code:
<iframe src="preview.html" title="Preview of the library notice"
        sandbox="" loading="lazy" referrerpolicy="no-referrer"
        width="640" height="360"></iframe>
explanation: An empty sandbox imposes restrictions without opting capabilities back in. This example needs a local preview.html and does not support a third-party widget that requires scripts or forms.
mistake: Adding every sandbox permission until an embed works, then assuming the original security boundary remains intact.
question: A widget needs only static text and images. Should you add allow-scripts and allow-same-origin by default?
answer: No. Do not grant capabilities without a demonstrated need. Test the actual static resource under the intended restrictions and document any permissions you choose to add.
objectives: Identify an embedding trust boundary
Choose sandbox permissions from actual requirements

title: Canvas, SVG and MathML
architecture_title: Canvas, SVG, MathML and graphics integration boundaries
part: V / Images, Audio, Video and Embedded Content
dek: Graphics need a document-level alternative strategy.
lesson:
canvas provides a bitmap drawing surface controlled through APIs. Drawing pixels does not automatically produce semantic headings, text or controls in the accessibility tree. Fallback content and a usable alternative interface need deliberate design.

SVG and MathML are foreign vocabularies that can be integrated into an HTML document. Their own element vocabularies and rules come from their respective specifications. HTML parsing and integration rules still matter at the boundary.

## Use the right representation
For a simple diagram, an SVG with a title and a text explanation can be more maintainable than a canvas rendering. For a data chart, an accessible table may communicate the exact values better than an image alone. For meaningful mathematical notation, MathML can express structure that a screenshot loses.

This chapter introduces the HTML integration. A complete Canvas 2D or SVG API reference requires separate member-level documentation and tests. Do not infer that a graphic is accessible merely because it has a title element. Review its purpose, interactions and the information the alternative actually supplies.
code:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 320 100"
     role="img" aria-labelledby="route-title route-desc">
  <title id="route-title">Route to the reading room</title>
  <desc id="route-desc">Reception connects directly to the reading room.</desc>
  <path d="M40 50 H280" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="4"/>
  <circle cx="40" cy="50" r="10" fill="currentColor"/>
  <circle cx="280" cy="50" r="10" fill="currentColor"/>
</svg>
explanation: The graphic has a short title and a description of the relationship. The visible diagram is intentionally simple. A real route plan with turns or hazards would need a more complete alternative.
mistake: Replacing an interactive chart with canvas pixels while removing all operable controls and data relationships.
question: Your canvas chart shows exact lending totals. What alternative lets readers inspect those values without interpreting pixels?
answer: Provide a text or data-table representation with the actual values and labels. Keep it synchronized with the chart data. If the chart has controls, those also need an accessible operable interface.
objectives: Distinguish bitmap drawing from document semantics
Describe HTML integration boundaries for foreign content

title: How forms send data
architecture_title: How HTML forms work
dek: Start with the request, then choose the controls.
lesson:
A form constructs an entry list from eligible controls and submits it according to its action, method and encoding rules. A visible input without a name usually does not contribute the expected name-value entry. An id connects labels and references; it is not the submission key.

GET commonly expresses retrieval by placing the encoded query in the URL. POST sends a request body under the selected encoding. Neither method provides encryption by itself. Use HTTPS for transport protection where appropriate and implement the server's validation, permissions and storage handling.

## Make the simple path work
A search form can submit without JavaScript. Build that path first when the service supports it. Scripts can enhance the experience without becoming the only way to reach the result.

Controls outside a form can be associated through a form attribute when their element supports it. Avoid relying on visual proximity as a submission relationship. Check actual submitted entries, including unchecked controls, disabled fields and the button used to submit. A browser preview without a backend cannot prove a successful application workflow.

## Predict the entry list
For an ordinary named text input, the name becomes the entry key and the current value becomes its value. A disabled control is omitted. An unchecked checkbox or radio button is omitted too; it does not automatically send a false value. A readonly text input can still contribute an entry. Repeated names can produce multiple entries, so do not assume that every form is a one-value-per-key object.

Give the server a deliberate interpretation for missing and repeated entries. Do not trust a disabled field, a hidden field or a client-side constraint to enforce a permission. Someone can construct a request without using your interface.
code:
<form action="catalogue.html" method="get">
  <label for="query">Search the catalogue</label>
  <input id="query" name="q" type="search">
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
explanation: The query key is q because that is the name. A real catalogue endpoint must read the query and return results; a static catalogue file does not implement that search service automatically.
mistake: Assuming that giving a control an id is enough to send its value under that key.
question: Why might a filled input appear on screen but be absent from the submitted entry list?
answer: It may lack a name, be disabled, be outside the relevant form without an association, or fall under another exclusion rule. Inspect the actual control state and form data rather than the visual layout.
objectives: Distinguish name from id
Explain a form request without inventing a backend

title: Labels and groups
architecture_title: Labels, fieldsets, legends and accessible grouping
dek: People should know what to enter before making a mistake.
lesson:
A label supplies the visible prompt for a form control. An explicit label uses for to reference the control's id. Nesting an appropriate control inside its label can also establish the association under the defined rules.

A placeholder is not a durable label. It can disappear as soon as someone types and often has poor contrast or confusing wording. Use supporting text for instructions, formatting rules and examples, then connect it with aria-describedby where that relationship helps.

## Group a shared question
fieldset and legend can express a group such as contact preference or membership type. Each radio still needs its own label. Keep the legend short enough that repeated announcements remain manageable.

Do not place essential instructions only in title or in a tooltip that requires a pointer. Write the instructions visibly. If a field is required, communicate that meaning consistently and explain the service's expectations. Required does not mean the requested information is necessary; review the form's data needs before adding fields.
code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>How should we contact you?</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="contact" value="email"> Email</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="contact" value="phone"> Phone</label>
</fieldset>
explanation: The shared name creates the radio group for submission and selection behavior. The legend supplies the common question. Each label names its own option.
mistake: Using two separate names for radio options that should be mutually exclusive.
question: Why does a legend not remove the need to label each radio button?
answer: The legend names the group question. Each radio still needs to identify its particular answer, such as Email or Phone. The reader needs both pieces of information.
objectives: Associate visible labels with controls
Group related choices with a fieldset and legend

title: Text, email and passwords
architecture_title: Text inputs, email, passwords and search
dek: Choose a state for the data, not just the keyboard.
lesson:
input type="text" is the general single-line text state. email and url have their own syntax and validation behavior. search can supply search-oriented interface behavior. password obscures the displayed value but does not encrypt it, protect it from scripts on the page or secure its eventual storage.

Use autocomplete tokens that describe the field's purpose. An existing-password field and a new-password field are different. Permit password managers and pasting rather than introducing unnecessary obstacles.

## Do not promise more validation than you have
An email input checks its defined syntax, not whether the address belongs to someone or can receive messages. A service that needs ownership verification must implement a separate confirmation process.

inputmode is a hint about input mechanisms, not a data validator. A numeric keyboard hint does not turn a text input into an integer or stop pasted characters. Pick constraints from the service's actual requirements, and keep server-side validation independent from the client interface.
code: We use this address to contact you about your application.
explanation: The helper describes this fictional form's intended use. Replace it with the actual service policy before collecting real addresses. The control cannot prove that a user controls the supplied mailbox.
mistake: Calling a password secure because its characters appear as dots, or disabling paste to discourage password managers.
question: Will type="email" prove that an address can receive your confirmation message?
answer: No. It applies the email state's syntax rules. Message delivery and ownership are application concerns that need their own process and error handling.
objectives: Choose a text-related input state
Distinguish syntax validation from verification

title: Numbers, dates and colour
architecture_title: Numeric, date, time, color and range inputs
dek: A control can normalize a value without deciding what it means.
lesson:
number fits quantities where numeric operations make sense. Do not use it for every string made of digits. A membership identifier or postal code may need leading zeros, nonnumeric characters or a format that should not change.

min, max and step affect constraints for relevant input states. A range control suits selecting within a range when approximate adjustment is appropriate. Give the value a meaningful visible context; a bare slider can leave readers unsure what they are choosing.

## Dates need a data model
date supplies a date without a timezone. datetime-local supplies a local date and time, also without an offset or timezone identifier. An appointment service needs a clear policy for interpreting that value. The displayed picker can vary across browsers while the submitted value follows defined syntax.

Colour controls and the newer alpha/colorspace attributes need their own implementation review. Do not assume every browser presents the same picker or supports every standardized extension. Keep a usable alternative when exact colour input is important.
code:
<label for="copies">Number of copies</label>
<input id="copies" name="copies" type="number" min="1" max="5" step="1">
<label for="visit-date">Preferred visit date</label>
<input id="visit-date" name="visitDate" type="date">
explanation: The quantity has integer steps within a range. The preferred date is not an instant on a global timeline and needs application interpretation before it becomes a scheduled event.
mistake: Using number for a phone number and losing formatting or leading-zero expectations.
question: Why is a phone number often better represented by type="tel" than type="number"?
answer: A phone number is an identifier with possible leading zeros, plus signs and formatting conventions. It is not a quantity to increment or average. tel can offer a useful input mechanism without pretending to validate every international number.
objectives: Distinguish quantities from numeric-looking identifiers
Interpret local dates without inventing timezones
