title: Choices, files and hidden values
architecture_title: Checkboxes, radio buttons, files and hidden inputs
dek: Submission depends on the control state.
lesson:
Checkboxes express independent choices. Radios with a shared name express a mutually exclusive selection. A checked checkbox or radio contributes its value under the defined entry-list rules; an unchecked one normally contributes no entry. Plan that absence on the server.

A file input lets a user choose files. accept is a hint to the chooser, not proof that a file is safe or of the declared type. File size, content, storage name and permissions need server-side checks. Do not serve uploaded files as executable content by accident.

## Hidden is not private
A hidden input participates in form submission without an ordinary visible control. Its value remains in the document and can be changed by a visitor. A server must not trust a hidden price, role or authorization decision merely because the page supplied it.

Likewise, readonly and disabled are different states for supporting controls. A readonly text control can still contribute its value; a disabled control is generally excluded from the entry list. Neither state is a substitute for enforcing business rules on the server.
code:
<label>
  <input type="checkbox" name="updates" value="yes">
  Email me the reading-group schedule
</label>
<label for="attachment">Supporting document</label>
<input id="attachment" name="attachment" type="file" accept=".pdf">
<input type="hidden" name="formVersion" value="1">
explanation: The hidden value is a routing hint for the application, not a trusted permission. A surrounding file-upload form needs the appropriate multipart encoding and a real upload handler.
mistake: Expecting an unchecked checkbox to submit the literal value false.
question: How should a server interpret the absence of an optional updates checkbox?
answer: Apply the documented default for the field, commonly not opted in. Do not infer consent from a missing value. Validate any submitted value as well, since clients can send requests without using the page.
objectives: Predict submitted entries for checked controls
Treat files and hidden values as untrusted input

title: Menus and longer text
architecture_title: Select menus, selectedcontent, options, datalists and textareas
dek: Choose the control that fits the number and kind of answers.
lesson:
select represents a choice among option elements, with optgroup available to group related choices. A native select carries behavior that a custom visual menu would otherwise need to recreate. Use a visible label and make any initial prompt consistent with required-selection rules.

textarea is for multiline text. Its initial value comes from its text content, not a value attribute. A datalist can supply suggestions for an associated input, but suggestions do not normally restrict the user to the listed values.

## Customizable selects need extra review
The Living Standard includes selectedcontent and newer customizable-select behavior. Their permitted structure and browser support need separate attention. Keep a conventional select usable as the baseline rather than assuming a decorative demonstration proves full keyboard and assistive-technology support.

multiple changes both the interface and submission expectations for a select. Do not use a multiple list solely to imitate the visual height of a different widget. Explain how to choose and how the service interprets several selected values.
code:
<label for="branch">Preferred branch</label>
<select id="branch" name="branch" required>
  <option value="">Choose a branch</option>
  <option value="central">Central</option>
  <option value="east">East</option>
</select>
<label for="request">What would you like to read?</label>
<textarea id="request" name="request" rows="4"></textarea>
explanation: This is a conventional select baseline. Its empty initial option works with the required single-select context shown here. Check the detailed placeholder-label rules before changing the structure.
mistake: Assuming datalist creates a strict allowed-value list or that textarea uses value like an input.
question: A field must accept only Central or East. Does an input with datalist enforce that restriction?
answer: No. A datalist provides suggestions. Use a suitable select for this choice and validate the submitted value on the server. A client can send any value regardless of the visible controls.
objectives: Use select, datalist and textarea intentionally
Keep a native baseline for newer select customization

title: Validation people can recover from
architecture_title: Native validation, constraints and error handling
dek: An error message should help someone finish the task.
lesson:
Native constraints include required, appropriate type rules and state-specific min, max, step, pattern and length restrictions. Their applicability differs by input state. A constraint in the wrong state may do nothing.

Constraint validation helps guide ordinary interaction. It does not secure a request. A server must validate the submitted data, enforce permissions and return useful errors even when JavaScript or browser validation has been bypassed.

## Keep the correction near the field
When application validation finds an error, identify the field and explain how to fix it. Preserve the submitted non-sensitive values when appropriate. Connect useful error text with aria-describedby and update aria-invalid when the application knows the value is invalid. Do not mark a field invalid before there is a reason to do so.

setCustomValidity can add an application message to supporting controls; a nonempty message keeps the control invalid until cleared. A mismatch between custom validity and visible errors can trap someone in a form. Test correction, not just failure. Native error UI varies between browsers, so do not base instructions on one screenshot.
code: Enter the six digits printed on your card.
explanation: The pattern applies to this text-state input. inputmode is a keyboard hint. The six-digit rule is fictional teaching policy and needs a matching server-side rule in a real service.
mistake: Adding a pattern without visible formatting guidance, or showing a generic Something went wrong message for a correctable field error.
question: After setting a custom validity message, a script sees the corrected value. What must it do to let the field become valid?
answer: Clear the custom message with setCustomValidity("") when the custom condition passes. Other native constraints may still apply, so inspect validity rather than assuming clearing one message proves every rule passed.
objectives: Apply state-specific constraints
Design and test the correction path

title: Submission and server boundaries
architecture_title: Submission methods, encoding, server integration and secure handling
dek: A finished form includes what happens after the request.
lesson:
Form submission produces an entry list and a request under defined rules. application/x-www-form-urlencoded is the common default encoding. File uploads through a conventional POST form need multipart/form-data. Do not choose text/plain as a general production data format merely because it looks readable.

A submit button can override supported submission attributes for that submission. The button used can also contribute its own name and value. Test these details when one form supports several actions.

## Protect and explain the result
Use server-side validation, appropriate authorization and protections suited to the application, including CSRF defenses where the authentication and request model need them. HTTPS protects transport; it does not decide whether the requester may change a record.

A successful HTTP response is not necessarily a successful business operation. Show whether the application accepted, rejected or queued the action, and explain the next step. Handle retries and duplicate submissions according to the service's data model. Static hosting serves the interface; a working submission service needs a separately implemented handler.

## Choose the submission path deliberately
Calling `form.requestSubmit()` runs the applicable constraint validation and, if submission proceeds, dispatches a `submit` event. Calling `form.submit()` directly bypasses that validation step and does not fire the `submit` event. Do not treat those methods as interchangeable shortcuts. Pass the intended submit button to `requestSubmit()` when its name, value or overrides matter.

For a multipart upload sent with `fetch` and `FormData`, let the browser generate the `Content-Type` boundary rather than hand-writing a bare multipart header. Read the service's expected request format and response contract before adapting a markup-only example. Use fictional data in local demonstrations. GET query values appear in the URL, and switching to POST does not replace HTTPS or careful logging and storage policies.
code:
<form action="/applications" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label for="proof">Address document</label>
  <input id="proof" name="proof" type="file" required>
  <button type="submit" name="action" value="apply">Send application</button>
</form>
explanation: The endpoint is illustrative and is not implemented by this static book. A real service needs a handler, storage rules, privacy information and testable success and failure states.
mistake: Claiming a contact or application form works because the browser renders the fields and button.
question: What else is required before this form can be advertised as accepting real applications?
answer: A working endpoint, validated and authorized handling, appropriate upload limits and storage controls, a clear privacy policy, and tested user-visible results for success, error and retry cases. Confirm deployment and transport behavior too.
objectives: Choose an encoding for the actual data
Separate a static form interface from its service

title: Buttons and commands
architecture_title: Buttons, commands and native interaction semantics
dek: A button should say what will happen.
lesson:
Use button for an action. Give it a clear name and choose type deliberately. A button associated with a form can submit by default in relevant states, so write type="button" for a local interface action and type="submit" for an intended submission.

A toggle button needs a represented state when the interaction is a persistent toggle. aria-pressed is appropriate for that pattern, not for every button that can be clicked. Keep the state synchronized with the result.

## Prefer a native action when it fits
The Standard includes command and commandfor for invoker commands, including relationships to dialogs and popovers under their defined rules. This can reduce script, but each command and target needs current compatibility review. Custom command names and their handling do not become application behavior automatically.

Avoid nesting another interactive control inside a button. An icon can accompany text, but a tooltip should not be the only way to discover an otherwise unnamed action. Disabled buttons are also a communication decision: if someone needs to know why they cannot continue, provide that explanation outside the unavailable control.
code:
<form action="catalogue.html" method="get">
  <label for="button-query">Book title</label>
  <input id="button-query" name="q" type="search">
  <button type="submit">Find books</button>
  <button type="reset">Clear the search</button>
</form>
explanation: The two types deliberately perform different native form operations. A reset button is shown to explain the behavior; decide whether clearing work is helpful enough to include in a real form.
mistake: Leaving a local interaction button without a type inside a form, then being surprised by submission.
question: Does a button that opens a dialog always need aria-pressed?
answer: No. aria-pressed represents a toggle-button state. A dialog opener is not automatically a toggle button. Give it an appropriate name and implement the dialog interaction and focus behavior correctly.
objectives: Choose a button type deliberately
Distinguish actions from persistent toggles

title: Disclosure with details
architecture_title: Disclosure widgets, details and summary
dek: Use a native disclosure before rebuilding one.
lesson:
details represents a disclosure. Its first summary supplies the label. The open attribute controls whether the contents are shown. This is a boolean attribute, so open="false" is still open.

A disclosure suits supplementary information that can reasonably remain collapsed. Do not hide the only instruction someone needs to complete a required field or understand a price behind an obscure label.

## Keep the summary useful
Write the summary as a question or a short description of the hidden information. Clicking it and keyboard activation should work without your own click handler. Avoid putting competing interactive controls in a summary without a specific reviewed reason.

The name attribute can associate details elements in an exclusive group under its defined behavior. Compatibility still matters. A group of disclosures is not automatically a tab interface or a full application accordion with every optional keyboard interaction from another pattern.

Test the disclosure with a keyboard and inspect whether its content is understandable when expanded. If you add animation, respect reduced-motion preferences and avoid delaying access to the actual information.
code:
Can I renew a borrowed book?

Ask the desk before the due date. Some collections have separate rules.
explanation: The summary remains the control. The paragraph is ordinary document content when the disclosure is open. The library rule is an illustrative example, not a real lending policy.
mistake: Adding role="button" and a second keyboard listener to a summary, creating duplicate or conflicting behavior.
question: How do you make this disclosure initially expanded, and how do you make it initially collapsed?
answer: Add open to details for an initially expanded disclosure. Omit open for the collapsed state. The string false is not a way to turn off the boolean attribute.
objectives: Use a native disclosure
Control a boolean open state correctly

title: Dialogs and popovers
architecture_title: Dialogs, popovers, close requests and related patterns
dek: Choose the interaction before choosing the container.
lesson:
A dialog can be shown modally with showModal or non-modally with show. A modal dialog changes interaction with the rest of the page. Opening it requires an intentional focus destination, a usable close path and sensible focus restoration when it closes.

Writing open in source displays a dialog in its non-modal open state; it does not reproduce every part of showModal. Use the dialog API or an appropriately supported invoker relationship for the intended behavior.

## A popover is not automatically a dialog
popover controls display and dismissal behavior for a popover element. It does not assign the semantics of a menu, dialog or tooltip. Choose markup and accessibility behavior for the actual content. The auto, manual and newer hint behaviors need their own defined handling and compatibility review.

closedby and declarative commands are newer parts of this area. Keep a compatible close mechanism and test Escape, focus, pointer dismissal and small-screen scrolling. Avoid using a modal merely to deliver a short message that could be shown in the page.

## Inspect the whole interaction
A modal dialog opened with `showModal()` makes the surrounding document inert under the defined modal-dialog rules. A popover does not make the rest of the document inert merely by being open. Neither feature supplies an appropriate accessible name for your content automatically. Give a dialog a meaningful name, choose its initial focus from the task and verify that closing leaves focus somewhere useful.

In the example, a valid form submission with `method="dialog"` closes its containing dialog rather than sending a network request. The activated submit button can supply the dialog's return value. That is a local interaction result, not confirmation that a server has saved anything.
code:
Membership help

Ask at the desk if you cannot supply an address document.
explanation: The close button submits the method="dialog" form, closing the dialog rather than posting to a server. Test the actual focus behavior and decide whether a more specific initial focus target is needed for longer content.
mistake: Assuming that adding the popover attribute supplies menu keyboard navigation or a dialog role.
question: Why is toggling the dialog open attribute not equivalent to calling showModal?
answer: showModal establishes modal behavior, including its relationship with the top layer and the rest of the page. The open attribute alone shows an open dialog without that same modal operation.
objectives: Distinguish modal dialog and popover behavior
Provide a keyboard-usable close path

title: Focus, editing and dragging
architecture_title: Editing, focus, selection, drag-and-drop and user interaction
dek: An interaction needs a path that does not depend on a pointer.
lesson:
Focusable and sequentially focusable are related but distinct. tabindex="0" can place an otherwise suitable element in sequential focus order. tabindex="-1" commonly allows programmatic focus without adding an ordinary tab stop. Positive tabindex values create a separate ordering problem and are usually best avoided.

contenteditable enables editing under its defined states. It does not provide a complete rich-text editor, accessible toolbar, sanitation pipeline or save system. Editing behavior and supported input methods need real-device testing.

## Offer alternatives to dragging
draggable participates in the drag-and-drop model. A drag gesture should not be the only way to perform an important operation. Provide buttons or another keyboard-usable mechanism for moving an item, and keep the outcome understandable.

Use focus to support a task, not to surprise someone whenever content changes. When removing a focused item, decide where focus goes next. Avoid trapping focus in a non-modal widget. Mobile input, speech control and assistive technology can expose assumptions that mouse-only testing misses.
code:
Your reading list

  1. Local histories
explanation: The heading can be a deliberate programmatic focus destination. The button demonstrates an alternative to a drag action, but its actual reordering logic is not implemented in this fragment.
mistake: Adding tabindex="0" to every paragraph and wrapper, making keyboard navigation unnecessarily long.
question: An item can only be moved by dragging. What should you add before treating the interaction as broadly usable?
answer: Provide an operable non-drag mechanism, such as Move up and Move down controls, then implement focus management and meaningful feedback for the result. Test with a keyboard and the actual input methods you support.
objectives: Explain sequential and programmatic focus
Provide a non-drag path for important actions

title: Templates and component boundaries
architecture_title: Templates, slots, custom elements and declarative shadow DOM
dek: A template stores a fragment without rendering it as ordinary page content.
lesson:
template holds inert template contents that a script can clone and insert. Its content is a DocumentFragment. Querying the template element's ordinary descendants is not the same as querying its content fragment.

slot is a placeholder within a shadow tree for assigned content. The slot attribute on an element identifies the named slot it should be assigned to under the relevant rules. This attribute is different from a slot element.

## Separate the pieces of a component
Autonomous custom elements use valid custom-element names, including the required hyphen and other naming restrictions, and are defined through the custom-elements machinery. A custom tag name alone does not register a working component. Customized built-in elements have separate is behavior and implementation considerations.

Declarative shadow DOM uses supported template shadowroot attributes to establish a shadow root during parsing under defined conditions. The evolving set includes mode, focus, cloning, serialization and registry-related controls. Review each independently. A shadow boundary is not a security sandbox or an excuse to ignore accessible names and keyboard behavior.
explanation: The example clones template content and inserts plain text into it. This is a template example, not a registered custom element or a shadow tree.
mistake: Treating a shadow root as protection against hostile same-page code, or treating a template string as safely sanitized HTML.
question: Why does the script use template.content rather than expecting the article to be a normal child rendered in the page?
answer: Template contents are held in a separate fragment and are not rendered as ordinary template children. Clone that fragment, fill it safely and insert it where the page should display it.
objectives: Clone inert template content
Distinguish templates, slots and custom-element registration

title: Custom data and structured data
architecture_title: Custom data attributes, microdata and structured content
dek: Store page-specific values without inventing semantics.
lesson:
data-* attributes store page-specific data where no more appropriate attribute fits. Scripts can access them through dataset with the defined name conversion. Values are strings; a value such as "false" is not automatically a false boolean.

Custom data is visible in the document. Do not place credentials or trusted authorization decisions there. A visitor can inspect and change it. Do not use a data attribute as a substitute for a real href, label or disabled state when the platform already defines one.

## Microdata serves a different purpose
itemscope, itemtype, itemprop, itemid and itemref participate in microdata. A vocabulary supplies meaning to properties; arbitrary names do not create a recognized public schema. Search and other consumers have their own supported formats and policies.

Keep visible content and structured annotations consistent. Do not claim that adding structured data guarantees a search result treatment. Choose a supported vocabulary and validate both its syntax and the content it represents using the relevant consumer's current documentation.
code:
<button type="button" data-book-id="LIB-204" id="save-book">
  Save Local histories
</button>
<script>
  const saveButton = document.getElementById("save-book");
  const bookId = saveButton.dataset.bookId;
  // Use bookId as an identifier, never as an authorization decision.
</script>
explanation: The conversion is from data-book-id to dataset.bookId. Reading an identifier does not save anything; a real action still needs its implementation and feedback.
mistake: Adding data-disabled="true" and expecting native disabled behavior.
question: What JavaScript type do you get from element.dataset.count when the source has data-count="3"?
answer: You get the string "3". Convert and validate it deliberately if your application needs a number. Do not trust the value merely because it appeared in your own initial markup.
objectives: Read custom data with explicit type handling
Distinguish page-specific data from public structured annotations

title: Global attributes in context
architecture_title: Global attributes in depth
dek: Global availability does not make every use a good idea.
lesson:
The global attributes section lists attributes common to HTML elements. DOM also owns requirements for id, class and slot. Other attributes and families integrate specifications such as ARIA and CSS Shadow Parts. Keep ownership and namespace boundaries clear.

An id must satisfy its defined authoring constraints and be unique among ids in the element's tree. class is a set of tokens. title supplies advisory information, but it is not a dependable sole label or instruction because exposure varies with device and interaction.

## Hidden and inert differ
hidden participates in rendering and relevance rules, including its until-found state in supporting implementations. inert prevents interaction and affects focus and accessibility exposure under its rules. Neither is simply a synonym for a CSS property.

Use lang and dir for their own meanings. accesskey can conflict with browser, operating-system or assistive-technology commands, so do not invent a keyboard shortcut scheme casually. Newer autocorrect, writingsuggestions and heading-level attributes need compatibility review. The reference keeps them visible rather than silently dropping them because they are unfamiliar.
code:
Renew your membership

Use the same name as your current library card.
explanation: id is a stable reference target. The two classes are separate tokens, not two independent class attributes. The section's language is explicit here even though it may already inherit English from html.
mistake: Relying on title as the only label for an icon-only control or the only explanation of a field error.
question: Can two unrelated controls safely share an id just because they are on different visual panels?
answer: Not within the same element tree. Visual separation does not establish a new id scope. Use unique ids and update all for, fragment and ARIA references consistently.
objectives: Apply global attributes with their own constraints
Keep id relationships unique and meaningful

title: Element-specific attributes
architecture_title: Element-specific attributes and valid values
dek: The same spelling can have different rules.
lesson:
An attribute name is not a complete definition. type means different things on input, button, script and other elements. value differs between a text input, an option and a progress element. Read the element and state alongside the name.

The reference retains contextual rows rather than merging everything into one alphabetical name list. An input's type can determine whether min, maxlength or another constraint applies. A parser accepting an attribute does not make the use conforming or effective.

## Check the default as well as the explicit value
Missing-value defaults and invalid-value defaults can differ. Enumerated attributes have defined keywords and states. Boolean attributes depend on presence. Token lists have their own constraints. When a script reflects an attribute through a property, the property can normalize or interpret it rather than exposing the raw source string.

For a new attribute, verify its canonical definition, supported elements, permitted values, side effects and implementation data. Preserve compatibility notes and fallback behavior. Do not infer support merely because getAttribute returns the text you set; the DOM can store unknown attributes too.
code:
<label for="age-years">Age in years</label>
<input id="age-years" name="age" type="number" min="0" max="120">
<label for="reader-name">Reader name</label>
<input id="reader-name" name="readerName" type="text" maxlength="100">
explanation: The numeric bounds suit the number state. The text length constraint suits the text state. These are illustrative service limits, not universal requirements for personal data.
mistake: Adding maxlength to a number input and assuming it enforces the number of digits.
question: Why does reading an unfamiliar attribute with getAttribute fail to prove native support?
answer: getAttribute reads stored attribute text. It does not demonstrate that the browser implements the attribute's specified behavior. Test the behavior and consult dated implementation evidence.
objectives: Interpret attributes in element and state context
Distinguish stored markup from implemented behavior

title: Metadata readers encounter
architecture_title: Titles, metadata, icons and document descriptions
dek: A good title helps someone find the right tab again.
lesson:
title identifies the document in browser UI and other contexts. Make it specific enough to distinguish this page from the rest of the site. A visible h1 and the document title have related but separate jobs.

meta can declare encoding or named metadata. A description is useful page-summary metadata, but its presence does not guarantee that a search engine will display it. Do not promise rankings from a tag.

## Keep head deliberate
Use link for supported resource relationships such as stylesheets and icons. A favicon is not the same as a visible logo. style holds embedded CSS when permitted. base changes URL resolution and target defaults, so use it only when you understand the effects on every relative reference.

Metadata names and link types have defined or registered meanings. Do not invent a plausible name and assume a consumer understands it. Social sharing formats also need their own current documentation. Keep canonical URLs accurate, and avoid adding several conflicting declarations through independently configured tools.
code: Visit and contact
explanation: The description summarizes this particular page. It makes no claim about search ranking or the exact snippet a service will show.
mistake: Giving every page the same title, or treating a meta description as a guaranteed search-result advertisement.
question: Which title better identifies the contact page: Welcome or Visit and contact | Neighbourhood Library?
answer: The second identifies both the page purpose and the site. It remains useful in a tab list, bookmark collection or history entry where surrounding page content is absent.
objectives: Write a specific document title
Describe metadata without search-result guarantees

title: Resource relationships
architecture_title: Links, resource hints and resource relationships
dek: rel tells consumers how a link relates to its context.
lesson:
A link relation gives a relationship meaning rather than merely a destination. link rel="stylesheet" requests a stylesheet relationship. An anchor's rel can annotate a hyperlink. Their allowed contexts and effects depend on the particular link type.

preload, preconnect and related hints should correspond to a real loading need. A preload has request details such as as and, when relevant, type or crossorigin. A mismatch with the eventual request can waste work rather than helping.

## Avoid hints by habit
Measure the loading problem before adding hints. A preconnect to a third party can create network and privacy costs even when the visitor never uses that service. A resource hint is not proof of a faster page.

Canonical, alternate, author and other relations have defined uses and consumer expectations. Keep the reference's link-type inventory separate from a list of attribute names. The rel attribute's existence does not enumerate all its possible relationship tokens or guarantee a particular consumer's action.
code:
<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">
<link rel="icon" href="favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">
explanation: These are head-context resource relationships. The resource files must exist at the resolved URLs. The example is displayed as source; the book's sandbox blocks external resource loading.
mistake: Preloading every image, font and script on a page without checking which resources are actually needed early.
question: Why might a preload download fail to benefit the later resource request?
answer: Its request parameters can differ from the later request, the resource may be unused, or the early work may contend with something more important. Inspect actual network behavior and request matching.
objectives: Read rel as a defined relationship
Evaluate hints using actual requests

title: Loading and policy attributes
architecture_title: Loading, fetching, referrer policies, integrity, nonces and priorities
dek: A hint and a security policy do not do the same job.
lesson:
loading and fetchpriority influence eligible loading decisions. They are not strict scheduling commands. crossorigin participates in the resource's fetching and CORS behavior; it does not grant your server permission to expose private data.

integrity integrates Subresource Integrity for supported resource uses. The hash must match the actual bytes, and cross-origin requirements matter. A placeholder digest is not a security control. nonce participates in a Content Security Policy arrangement and should be generated and delivered according to that policy's requirements.

## Follow the actual authority
HTML defines where these attributes integrate, while Fetch, CORS, CSP, Referrer Policy and SRI own important parts of their behavior. Read the relevant specification and deployment documentation for a security assertion.

referrerpolicy controls referrer information according to the defined policy, not all information a remote service can learn. Avoid presenting one attribute as a complete privacy solution. Test response headers and real requests as well as the source markup.
code: Read the example partner's list
explanation: The example demonstrates a referrer policy on a hyperlink. It does not remove the network request, hide the destination from the visitor's network, or imply a relationship with an actual partner.
mistake: Copying a static nonce into every deployment and describing it as a complete CSP configuration.
question: Can adding crossorigin make a remote server return private data to your script when that server does not allow the origin?
answer: No. The server's CORS policy and the request mode and credentials behavior still apply. The attribute is part of a fetching configuration, not a bypass for a server's access policy.
objectives: Distinguish loading hints from policy enforcement
Trace integration claims to the owning specification

title: Attributes and properties
architecture_title: Attribute reflection, defaults and browser interpretation
dek: Source text, defaults and current state can diverge.
lesson:
getAttribute reads an attribute's text or returns null when absent. A corresponding DOM property can expose a parsed, normalized or stateful value. Do not assume they always remain equal.

For a text input, the value attribute is associated with its default value, while the value property describes the current value under the control's rules. User edits can change the current value without rewriting the source attribute. checked and defaultChecked have a related distinction for appropriate controls.

## Read the right layer
Boolean reflection commonly maps property true to attribute presence and false to absence. URL properties can return resolved absolute URLs while the attribute contains a relative string. Numeric reflection has its own rules, defaults and limits.

When debugging, ask whether the question concerns the original source, the current attribute, or the current control state. Reset behavior, script assignment and user interaction can affect different layers. Avoid a generic helper that treats every attribute and property as interchangeable strings.
code:
<label for="nickname">Reading-group name</label>
<input id="nickname" name="nickname" value="Guest">
<script>
  const field = document.getElementById("nickname");
  field.value = "Ada";
  console.log(field.value);                 // Ada
  console.log(field.getAttribute("value")); // Guest
</script>
explanation: The script changes the current input value. The attribute retains Guest in this example. This is a specific input-state behavior, not a universal rule for every property named value.
mistake: Using getAttribute("value") to read a text field after the user has edited it.
question: Which should an ordinary script read for the current text input value after editing?
answer: Read the input's value property. If you need the default value or the raw attribute, ask for that specifically instead of assuming it equals the current state.
objectives: Distinguish raw attributes and current state
Read the correct layer when debugging controls

title: How parsing starts
architecture_title: HTML parsing and tokenization
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: The parser has states, not a general find-and-replace rule.
lesson:
HTML parsing includes tokenization and tree construction. The tokenizer recognizes text, tags, attributes, comments and other tokens while its state affects how characters are interpreted. A less-than sign inside an ordinary text context does not have the same surrounding rules as text in script or style.

Character references are consumed in the contexts defined by the parser. An apparent tag inside a JavaScript string can still interact with the HTML script-data rules, which is why serializing arbitrary data into inline script needs careful escaping and a reviewed approach.

## Do not sanitize with a tag regex
Untrusted HTML needs a context-appropriate safe handling strategy. Plain text should usually be inserted as text. If a product truly accepts markup, use a maintained sanitizer configured for the allowed content and review how it interacts with the destination.

Encoding for one context does not automatically encode for another. An HTML attribute, JavaScript string, URL and CSS value have different grammar. The examples here are educational text; they are not a complete sanitizer implementation.
explanation: The literal string appears as text because the script assigns textContent. It does not create a strong element. Use this route when the product accepts text rather than markup.
mistake: Assuming that stripping text between angle brackets with a regular expression produces safe HTML.
question: If a comment field is intended to accept plain text, why use textContent rather than innerHTML?
answer: textContent creates text without interpreting the submitted string as markup. innerHTML parses markup and can introduce dangerous behavior if the data is not handled with a correct sanitization strategy.
objectives: Describe tokenizer context
Choose text insertion for plain untrusted text

title: Tree construction and recovery
architecture_title: Tree construction and error recovery
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: Inspect what the browser built, then fix the source.
lesson:
The tree builder processes tokens using insertion modes and special rules. Table parsing, implied end tags and misnested formatting are examples where a browser can build a tree that differs from an author's naive reading of the source.

Error recovery is specified so browsers can process existing pages consistently. It is not a list of recommended authoring shortcuts. A source file can appear usable while the parsed relationships break labels, selectors or accessibility semantics.

## Make a small failing case
Reduce unexpected markup to the shortest document that still produces the surprising tree. Compare View Source with the live DOM. Remove scripts and extensions that might be modifying the result before blaming parsing.

Keep invalid examples explicitly labelled. When a checker reports a problem, record the intended correction and verify the resulting tree. Add a regression test for the relationship that mattered, not just a screenshot of the page.
code:
Applications are open.

How to apply

Collect a form at the desk.
explanation: This corrected structure keeps the section outside the paragraph. A paragraph cannot be used as a generic container for the whole notice, even if recovery makes the output look plausible.
mistake: Testing a CSS selector against the intended source hierarchy rather than the hierarchy the parser actually created.
question: How should you investigate a table row that appears in an unexpected place in Developer Tools?
answer: Create a reduced complete document, inspect its actual DOM and check the source against table content rules. Parsing can relocate or imply nodes. Verify the correction with a checker and a DOM assertion.
objectives: Observe a repaired tree without recommending invalid source
Reduce parsing bugs to a testable fixture

title: The document lifecycle
architecture_title: DOM interfaces and document lifecycle
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: Wait for the condition your code actually needs.
lesson:
The document moves through loading states. DOMContentLoaded relates to parsing and eligible deferred/module script execution. The load event waits for the document's relevant dependent resources. Neither event proves that every later asynchronous operation has completed.

A script placed after a target element can often use that element immediately. A deferred external classic script runs after parsing under its ordering rules. Code that can run after DOMContentLoaded has already fired may need to inspect readyState before deciding whether to attach a listener.

## Separate readiness from data
A catalogue fetch completing is an application condition, not the same as the initial DOM being ready. Give the result area explicit loading, empty, error and success states where needed. Do not leave a spinner indefinitely because a request failed.

Document navigation, visibility changes, page restoration and the back-forward cache introduce further lifecycle cases. Avoid using unload as a dependable save system. Design persistence and recovery around the actual platform behavior and test reload and back navigation.
code: Preparing the catalogue view.
explanation: This pattern handles running before or after initial parsing has finished. It announces only that this local view initialization ran, not that remote catalogue data was fetched.
mistake: Waiting for load for every DOM task, or assuming DOMContentLoaded waits for every image and application request.
question: What should your code wait for before rendering data from a specific fetch request?
answer: Wait for that request and its response processing, then render or show its error state. Document readiness alone does not prove the data is available.
objectives: Choose a readiness condition
Separate document lifecycle from application data loading

title: Scripts and execution
architecture_title: Script loading, execution, import maps and integration
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: Order, dependencies and origin rules affect the result.
lesson:
An ordinary external classic script without async or defer can block parsing while it is fetched and executed. defer allows eligible external classic scripts to run after parsing, preserving their deferred execution order. async allows independent loading and execution without that dependency ordering guarantee.

Module scripts have their own loading, dependency, scope and CORS behavior. They are deferred by default in the usual parser-inserted case. Do not assume that adding type="module" to an existing global script preserves every behavior.

## Give dependency rules a home
If one script relies on another, represent the dependency through an appropriate module graph or a deliberately ordered loading strategy. Import maps define supported module-specifier mappings under their own processing rules. Newer script types, including speculation rules, need their own review.

noscript provides content for defined scripting-disabled cases. It is not a catch-all for script download failures or runtime exceptions. A progressively enhanced page should keep useful content and a clear failure path even when one script fails.

## Check which rules apply
For a classic script, `defer` is useful on an external script with `src`; adding it to an inline classic script does not defer that inline code. An async script must tolerate running when its own download is ready rather than relying on document order. Keep shared setup explicit instead of hoping the network will deliver files in the right order.

Module code runs in strict mode and has module scope. Top-level declarations do not become window properties merely because the module is loaded by a page. Check any code that expects globals, and test a failed dependency as well as the successful path.
code: The complete book list is available on the catalogue page.
explanation: The file catalogue.js must exist and implement its behavior. The noscript fallback concerns disabled scripting; a failed request for catalogue.js still needs a resilient baseline or another failure strategy.
mistake: Using async on two dependent classic scripts and relying on their tag order for execution order.
question: Would noscript automatically display when a script downloads successfully but throws an exception?
answer: No. Scripting remains enabled. Handle the failure in the application design and keep a useful underlying document instead of relying on noscript for runtime errors.
objectives: Choose a loading strategy for dependencies
Distinguish disabled scripting from script failure

title: HTML and XML serialization
architecture_title: HTML/XML differences, XHTML and serialization
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: The media type changes the parser and its rules.
lesson:
HTML syntax and XML syntax are not interchangeable decorations around the same file. A response's media type determines the relevant processing path. Renaming a file or adding an XHTML-looking namespace does not make a text/html response use XML parsing.

In HTML, element and attribute processing includes defined case handling and error recovery. XML has different well-formedness, namespace and case rules. An XML parse error is not handled like an ordinary recoverable HTML authoring error.

## Do not infer a mode from a slash
A trailing slash on br in HTML is not the XML mechanism applied to every element. A non-void HTML element still needs its end tag. Conversely, XML serialization has its own namespace and empty-element rules.

If you intentionally serve application/xhtml+xml, test the actual HTTP Content-Type and XML requirements. For normal HTML authoring in this book, use the short HTML doctype, UTF-8 and text/html. Preserve namespace-sensitive behavior when integrating SVG or MathML.
code:
Neighbourhood Library
Reading room entrance
explanation: This is intended as text/html. The br element is void and does not have an end tag. A local browser file test is not proof of the headers used by a deployed server.
mistake: Adding xmlns to html and assuming it switches the HTML parser to XML mode.
question: Which matters more for choosing the HTML or XML parsing path: an XHTML-looking source style or the actual response media type?
answer: The actual processing context and response media type matter. Confirm the server behavior and follow the rules for that syntax; visual resemblance to XHTML is insufficient.
objectives: Distinguish HTML and XML processing
Test the media type rather than guessing from source style

title: HTML and rendering
architecture_title: Rendering behavior and HTML's relationship with CSS
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: Default styles are a starting point, not the meaning.
lesson:
Browsers have default rendering rules and styles. A heading often appears bold and large; an anchor often appears underlined. Those defaults make an unstyled document usable, but they do not define every semantic or accessibility behavior.

Changing display can alter layout without changing the element's underlying HTML definition. It can also interact with accessibility mappings and implementation quirks. Test the actual result rather than assuming a CSS property is semantically harmless everywhere.

## Keep reading order deliberate
Layout can visually reorder items while the DOM order stays the same. A keyboard or screen reader may encounter a sequence unlike the visual arrangement. Put the logical order in HTML and use layout to adapt it without creating competing stories.

Use HTML attributes with their intended behavior rather than recreating them through presentation alone. CSS hiding, hidden and inert have different consequences. Contrast, focus visibility, reflow and zoom are also part of the usable page, even though their implementation often lives in CSS.
code:
Visit the reading room

Check the current opening hours before travelling.

Read the opening hours
explanation: The source remains a sensible reading sequence before layout. Styling should not move the link ahead of its context solely to match a decorative composition.
mistake: Choosing an element because its browser default margin looks right, then compensating for the wrong semantics with ARIA.
question: Can CSS make an h2 look larger than an h1 without changing their heading levels?
answer: Yes. Presentation and heading rank are different. Keep the semantic hierarchy appropriate and use CSS for the visual scale, then check that the overall design still communicates the structure.
objectives: Distinguish default appearance from meaning
Keep source and interaction order understandable

title: Where the wider APIs begin
architecture_title: Web-platform APIs, communication, workers, worklets and storage: integration overview
part: IX / Browser Processing and Advanced Concepts
dek: Know the boundary before calling the reference exhaustive.
lesson:
The HTML Standard includes more than markup. It defines navigation and history behavior, messaging, workers, worklets, storage, event loops and many interfaces. A language guide can introduce their integration, but a named-interface list does not document every member or algorithm.

localStorage is synchronous, origin-scoped storage with its own access and failure behavior. It is not a suitable place for secrets simply because it is local. Workers run script in a different execution environment, not a second DOM you can manipulate directly. Messaging needs explicit origin and data validation where relevant.

## Treat integration as a design decision
A history update needs a corresponding content and navigation strategy. A cross-document message needs an expected sender and validated payload. A background task needs cancellation and failure handling. These responsibilities do not disappear because the API call is short.

## What the catalogue actually contains
The foundation catalogue retains 166 named interface discovery routes. The expanded declaration register separately records 314 named WebIDL declaration owners and 1,574 direct member declarations in the captured source. Owners include more than interfaces, and direct declarations do not expand every inherited member. These are different inventories, not competing counts of the same thing.

Use the declaration register for signatures and links to definitions. A declaration alone does not explain an algorithm, an exception, an event sequence or a security boundary. Some member links deliberately fall back to their owning definition and are labelled accordingly. Whole-Standard behavioral coverage, imported cross-specification APIs and independent review remain open.

Storage can fail. Access may be restricted by the document's origin or browser policy, and writes can fail when storage limits are reached. Keep the page usable when a preference cannot be saved. Do not assume that a successful write is a durable backup or that any script running in the same origin is barred from reading the stored data.
explanation: Storage can be unavailable or fail. The book's isolated example sandbox may not allow localStorage, so the failure path is intentional. No data is sent to a server.
mistake: Calling a reference complete because every interface name appears somewhere in it.
question: Why does the example catch a storage failure rather than assuming localStorage is always writable?
answer: Access restrictions, browser settings and storage failures can prevent writing. A preference control should remain usable and explain the actual result. Do not report a successful save when the write failed.
objectives: Identify wider API responsibilities
Keep API integration separate from member-level completeness

title: Accessibility starts in the markup
architecture_title: Accessible HTML and WCAG-oriented implementation
dek: Semantic HTML helps, but it does not certify the whole experience.
lesson:
Use native elements that fit the task, then review the name, role, state and behavior actually exposed to users. A button needs an understandable name and an operable action. A heading needs a useful position in the document hierarchy. A table needs its data relationships.

ARIA can supplement semantics where needed. It can also introduce wrong or conflicting information. Follow ARIA in HTML restrictions rather than adding roles to every element. Prefer an existing visible label through a native label relationship or a suitable reference before inventing an unrelated hidden name.

## Review the entire task
A successful automated scan does not demonstrate WCAG conformance. Test keyboard operation, visible focus, text alternatives, error correction, zoom, reflow and appropriate assistive-technology behavior. Include the actual data and content states, not just a polished empty page.

WCAG describes requirements at the level of the delivered experience. HTML-AAM, AccName, WAI-ARIA and ARIA in HTML help answer more specific mapping and authoring questions. This edition links to them but has not completed an independent accessibility audit. Record that limitation instead of turning a few semantic examples into a certification badge.
code:
<form action="catalogue.html" method="get">
  <label for="accessible-search">Search books by title</label>
  <input id="accessible-search" name="q" type="search">
  <button type="submit">Search books</button>
</form>
explanation: The visible label, control relationship and button text support an understandable task. You still need a functioning search response, usable focus styles and tested result/error states in the real service.
mistake: Adding an aria-label that contradicts the visible wording, or describing role-based automated tests as a complete accessibility review.
question: A scanner reports no issues. What should you do before claiming that the search experience is accessible?
answer: Complete the relevant manual and assistive-technology checks across the actual task and states, assess applicable WCAG requirements, and document results and limitations. A scanner result is one piece of evidence.
objectives: Use native semantics with accurate names
Separate automated checks from accessibility conformance

title: Keyboard and focus review
architecture_title: Keyboard navigation, focus and assistive technology
dek: Follow the task without touching the mouse.
lesson:
Begin at the top of the page and use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space and the keys appropriate to each native control. Confirm that every needed action is reachable, the order is sensible and focus remains visible.

Do not require hover to reveal the only route to an action. A control that appears on pointer hover should have an equivalent usable focus or interaction path. Keep focus indications strong enough to locate rather than removing outlines without a replacement.

## Check transitions, not just tab stops
Open and close a dialog. Submit an invalid form. Remove a focused list item. Load more results. These transitions need deliberate focus and feedback behavior. Moving focus on every update can be as disruptive as losing it.

A disabled control and an aria-disabled control do not automatically behave the same way. ARIA communicates semantics but does not implement all interaction restrictions. Choose the appropriate element/state and test the actual behavior.

Record the browser, operating system and assistive technology used. A successful keyboard pass in one environment is useful evidence, not a claim about all combinations.
code:

explanation: This is a starting structure. The stylesheet must keep the skip link discoverable on focus, and the Add a book action still needs its implementation and focus plan.
mistake: Setting a positive tabindex sequence to match a visual layout instead of fixing the source order.
question: After deleting the focused row in a list, where should focus go?
answer: There is no universal target. Choose a predictable nearby control or a relevant list heading based on the task, then test the behavior. Do not let focus disappear into the document body accidentally.
objectives: Run a task-based keyboard check
Plan focus after dynamic changes

title: Trust boundaries
architecture_title: Security, safe embedding, trust boundaries and policy integration
dek: Treat browser input as something the server must verify.
lesson:
A browser can display constraints and hidden values, but a requester can send a different request. Validate on the server, enforce the relevant authentication and authorization rules, and apply abuse controls appropriate to the service.

For content insertion, distinguish plain text from accepted markup. textContent fits text. Markup acceptance needs a maintained, context-appropriate sanitization strategy. A handmade list of forbidden strings is not a dependable general sanitizer.

## Review each boundary
A form crosses into a server handler. An iframe crosses into another document. A script can introduce a remote execution dependency. A file upload crosses into storage and later retrieval. Document the expected origin, allowed capabilities and validation for each boundary.

Security policies and headers belong to the deployment as well as the document. CSP, CORS, SRI, referrer policy and Permissions Policy address different concerns. Do not describe any one of them as a complete defense. Test the intended failure behavior, and never place private API credentials in HTML, client JavaScript, data attributes or a downloadable environment file.
explanation: The comment is rendered as text. Splitting the closing script spelling here avoids accidentally terminating the surrounding HTML script element. Real serialization should use a reviewed data-embedding strategy.
mistake: Thinking that a value is trusted because it originated in a hidden input or a front-end build variable.
question: Why must the server ignore a submitted role="admin" value when deciding a requester's permissions?
answer: The requester controls submitted data. Authorization must use trusted server-side identity and permission information, not a role string supplied by the client.
objectives: Identify client-controlled data
Choose controls for specific trust boundaries

title: Performance without folklore
architecture_title: Performance, loading behavior and media optimization
dek: Find the slow resource before adding an optimization.
lesson:
HTML influences resource discovery and loading. An early stylesheet link, a delayed image source, script loading attributes and image candidates can affect the page's critical work. Measure the actual page on representative conditions before prescribing changes.

Provide image dimensions and appropriate resources. Keep likely important above-the-fold media from being needlessly delayed. Lazy loading is useful when deferring a resource is appropriate; it is not a rule to apply to every image.

## Test a before and an after
Record the page version, device or emulation, network conditions and measurement method. Repeat enough to recognize variation. Do not invent percentage improvements or treat one warm-cache result as a stable performance guarantee.

A fast initial response can coexist with a slow interaction. Loading less script helps only when it addresses actual work. Keep the underlying document usable while enhancements load. Review the network waterfall and interaction path together rather than optimizing a score in isolation.
explanation: A high priority hint can be appropriate for an important image, but only when the page and measured loading behavior justify it. This filename is an illustrative resource, not an image included in the example sandbox.
mistake: Claiming that fetchpriority="high" on every image makes the page faster.
question: What evidence should accompany a claim that an HTML loading change improved performance?
answer: A recorded before/after measurement under stated comparable conditions, with the tested page version and enough detail to reproduce it. Explain variability and avoid generalizing beyond the measured scenario.
objectives: Relate HTML loading choices to real resources
Report measured results with their conditions

title: Findable and shareable pages
architecture_title: SEO, metadata and structured content
dek: Describe the page accurately before chasing a search treatment.
lesson:
Use descriptive titles, meaningful headings and links, useful body content and accurate metadata. A crawler cannot discover a resource through a private thought or a button whose only destination exists in opaque application state.

Canonical URLs should identify the intended canonical document, not point every page to the home page. Alternate-language relationships need correct URLs and language relationships. Structured data should match the visible content and an actual supported vocabulary.

## Keep promises narrow
A meta description can help summarize a page but does not force a search snippet. Structured data does not guarantee a rich result. Social-card previews depend on platform behavior, caching and the accessible resource URLs.

Test the deployed output, not only templates. A robots restriction, a wrong status code, an inaccessible asset or a repository subpath error can undo otherwise tidy head markup. Do not add a measurement claim or an SEO guarantee to sales copy without actual evidence.

## Discovery is not access control
A crawler needs to fetch a page to read its `noindex` instruction. Blocking that fetch in `robots.txt` is not a reliable way to make the crawler process the page's noindex metadata. Neither directive protects private information. Use actual authentication and authorization for private content.

An `llms.txt` file can offer a plain-text route through a publication, but it is not a universal crawler protocol or a promise of inclusion in AI answers. Keep any discovery export consistent with the visible book. Search visibility, snippet choice and model use remain outside the publisher's control.
code:
How to renew your library membership

Check the documents you need before visiting the desk.

Documents accepted for renewal
explanation: The heading and link describe a specific task. The actual accepted-document page must exist and give current information. HTML alone does not ensure indexing or ranking.
mistake: Using the same generic summary and title on every page, then adding unsupported ranking claims.
question: Does a valid canonical link prove that a search engine will choose your preferred URL?
answer: No. It supplies a signal that consumers interpret under their own rules. Keep the signal accurate and consistent with redirects, links and actual content, then inspect the deployed behavior.
objectives: Write task-specific titles and links
Qualify metadata and search-consumer claims

title: Maintainable HTML
architecture_title: Internationalization, maintainability and progressive enhancement
dek: A useful baseline makes later changes less fragile.
lesson:
Keep the content, relationships and primary task available before adding optional enhancements where the service permits it. Progressive enhancement is a design approach, not a promise that every application can offer identical behavior without scripting.

Use consistent naming, a small number of clear components and maintained sources for repeated structures. Avoid editing separate website and PDF copies of the same explanation. A single-source build reduces drift, but the generated outputs still need independent checks.

## Plan for changed content
Test a long name, a translated label, no results, a server error and more content than the design screenshot contained. A layout that only works with one short English phrase is not ready for real users.

Keep source review dates, compatibility notes and meaningful changelog entries. A Living Standard and browser implementations can change independently. Assign an actual maintainer before promising updates. Do not advertise an automated maintenance process that has not been configured.

explanation: A real endpoint can support a conventional form submission. A script may add in-page results, while the browse link provides another route. A static file with no query handler is not automatically that endpoint.
mistake: Calling a page progressively enhanced when every visible route silently depends on one script succeeding.
question: What content states should you test besides the short, successful example shown in a design file?
answer: Include empty, loading, error, long-content, translated and high-density states as relevant to the task. Test the actual interaction and recovery path, not just their appearance.

title: A release checklist that means something
architecture_title: Validation, browser testing, code review and production checklists
dek: An unchecked box is an open task, not a smaller font.
lesson:
Check the built documents with a recorded checker version. Test internal links and referenced assets under the real deployment base path. Inspect the browser console and run behavior tests for the examples that make behavior claims.

Review keyboard navigation, focus, names, text alternatives, form errors, reflow and relevant assistive-technology use. Record what was tested and what was not. Security and accessibility reviews need named responsibilities and evidence rather than decorative badges.

## Separate authoring from approval
An answer being written does not mean it has been independently checked. A chapter existing does not mean every assigned feature is fully documented. Keep drafting, example conformance, browser behavior, compatibility and editorial approval as separate states.

For publication, verify the PDF's text, links, navigation and accessibility workflow; do not call an untagged export an accessible PDF. Check downloads in a logged-out browser and test the promised delivery method. The published reading edition keeps its executed checks and open reviews separate. Being available on the web does not mean every whole-Standard coverage gate has closed.

## Record an observation, not a badge
A useful release note identifies the artifact, the date, the tool or browser, the action performed and the observed result. "The homepage loaded" is useful delivery evidence, but it says nothing about an untested registration handler. "Zero automated accessibility violations" describes that scan, not a complete keyboard or screen-reader review. Keep the original limits beside the result so the next reader knows what still needs testing.

For this book, report corrections with the chapter or reference URL, the passage, a reproducible example when relevant and the source that supports the proposed change. Do not include personal form data, private credentials or unpublished security details in a public issue.
code:
Before publishing

  • Validate the built documents and record the output.
  • Test the main tasks with a keyboard.
  • Check paths under the deployment subdirectory.
  • Record remaining content and technical review work.
explanation: This is a visible checklist, not an assertion that its tasks passed. A project should link each claimed result to the relevant command output, environment or review note.
mistake: Renaming a draft final and carrying its unchecked review states into the release unchanged.
question: What should you do if examples validate but the API-member inventory is incomplete?
answer: Report the example result separately, keep API coverage open, and limit the publication promise or complete the missing inventory before making the broader claim. One passing check cannot close unrelated work.
objectives: Keep independent review states
Tie release claims to specific evidence

title: Build an article page
architecture_title: Build an article and documentation page
dek: Make long content navigable without turning every paragraph into a card.
lesson:
Build a documentation article called How lending works. Include a page title, introduction, an on-page contents list, three meaningful sections and an update date. Use time only when you can supply the appropriate machine-readable value.

The contents links must point to unique section ids. Keep heading levels consistent. An aside can hold genuinely supporting material, such as a definition of an unfamiliar term, but not the only copy of essential renewal instructions.
